The Company’s main activity is the wholesale and retail sale of food, clothing and products in general through its stores under the commercial brand “Tía” focused on serving the customers at the base of the pyramid.</p>
<p><br />
Through the Transaction, IDB Invest seeks to enable financing under competitive conditions for Tiendas TÍA’s suppliers, which are mostly MSMEs, in Ecuador by discounting or monetizing their credit rights arising from the sale of goods and/or services to Tiendas TÍA. <br />
 </p>

<p>The proposed operation consists of the financing of: (i) the development, construction, operation and maintenance of a portfolio of distributed generation assets in Jamaica, including ground mounted, rooftop and carport solar photovoltaic (“PV”) installations as well as energy storage solutions and interconnection facilities (each, an “Installation”) with an initial aggregate generating capacity of approximately 11.25 mega-watt peak (“MWp”), which will be contracted with commercial and industrial clients through long-term lease contracts (“Phase I”); and (ii) a subsequent set of Installations for additional generation capacity following the same long-term leasing structure (“Phase II”). Together, (i) and (ii) are the “Project”. The construction period is expected to be no longer than 12 months. The Project developer, Soleco Energy Limited (“SEL” or the “Company”) manages the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (“EPC”) and Operations and Maintenance (“O&amp;M”) works contracted to Grupotec Servicios Avanzados, S.A. (or “Grupotec”) for Phase I of the Project.&nbsp;</p>

<p><span><span>Belize Electricity Limited (“The Client,” “The Company,” or “BEL”) is the primary distributor of electricity in Belize, Central America. Its aggregate energy sales in 2020 was 539.3 gigawatt-hours (GWh) to a approximately 104,000 customers with peak power demand of 102.7 megawatts (MW) during the year. The Client is seeking funds to cover both short-term working capital needs as well as to pay for scheduled capital projects. Phase I of the operation will provide financing for a working capital tranche and finance capex including equipment, software, system development, infrastructure upgrade works and customer services (the “Project”). Other Phases of the operation will be assessed in the future in terms of their potential environmental and social impacts.&nbsp; </span></span></p>

<p>In February 2021, within the framework of a broad agreement between the Government of the Eastern Republic of Uruguay and Katoen Natie ("KN"), the majority shareholder of <a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-supports-expansion-port-…;, these parties agreed to expand the infrastructure of the specialized container terminal of the port of Montevideo. According to present estimates, the Borrower will invest an amount exceeding US$600 million in order to position the port as a regional and competitive Hub in the region. Said investment will contemplate, among the most significant, the following: ( i) new gantry cranes and horizontal transfer equipment; (ii) expansion and modernization of truck access at the Terminal; (iii) new paving of the original container yard; and (iv) new computer systems.</p><p>Once the works are completed, the port of Montevideo will have a specialized state-of-the-art container terminal, which will at least double its annual capacity and will allow it to serve the most modern ships (400m). The two docks, which will total more than 1,300m, will allow TCP to operate 4 container ships simultaneously. Likewise, this increase in capacity and concentration of cargo will improve the efficiency of the operation and reduce costs per container, with the aim of placing Montevideo in a privileged place on the map of transit cargo exchange routes. and transshipment, consolidating its strategic position and attracting cargo to said port.</p>

The Fund will be managed by Accion International (“Accion” or the “Fund Manager”), a pioneer in the microfinance sector with over 50 years of global experience in this segment.</span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p><span><span><span><span><span>The COVID- 19 pandemic has increased the financial gap for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises ("MSMEs") and has specifically affected women, who represent the majority of MFI borrowers. </span></span></span></span></span></p>

(the “Fund Manager”). <p><span>Renewstable (Barbados) Inc. <p>The <a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-supports-road-infrastruc…; target="_blank">Santana – Mocoa – Neiva corridor</a> (the “Project”) is part of the fourth-generation (“4G”) concessions program headed by the Colombian government through its National Infrastructure Agency (“ANI”). description:
<p><span><span><span>The Project objective is to increase the access to Climate Finance solutions to mid-market companies in Latin America and the Caribbean ("LAC") through the provision of tailored long-term growth financing solutions for climate investments to mitigate and adapt to Climate Change impacts across the region.</span></span></span></p>
<p><span><span><span><span><span>The Project consists of an IDB Invest investment of up to US$50 million in the <a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-contribute-climate-chang…; target="_blank">DIC Latin American Fund IV, L.P.</a> (“LAC Green Debt Fund” or the “Fund”), the first private credit climate finance fund in LAC. </span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p><span><span><span><span><span>The Fund will be managed by Darby International Capital (“Darby” or the “Manager”), an independent investing firm, founded in 2020 as a result of the team spinning-off from Franking Templeton’s private debt arm, focused on private credit solutions for mid-market companies across LAC. Darby’s management team is led by Richard H. Frank Jr. and Ignacio Aicardi, both seasoned investors and former heads of Franklin Templeton private credit strategy in LAC.</span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p><span><span><span><span><span>With a target size of US$450 million, the Fund’s investment strategy is built around providing tailored credit solutions to around 10-12 mid-market companies (with EBITDAs of US$5 million-US$20 million), consisting mainly in senior secured loans with equity kickers (i.e., warrants, income participation, among others). The Fund will be focused on financially sound companies with natural currency hedges, proven management track records, moderate operating and financial risk profiles, and strong competitive positions within their respective sectors, but lacking adequate financing for its business model and expansion plans. The Fund will invest at least 30% of the portfolio in climate investments, with an aspirational target of 50%. The Fund will have a five-year investment period and a total life of 10 years, with the possibility of two one-year extensions. </span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p><span><span><span><span><span>The Fund can play a key role in developing tailored Climate Finance solutions for mid-market companies across LAC’s private credit market to support sustainable economic growth while mobilizing local and international investors’ capital towards the advancement of the Climate Finance agenda in the region.</span></span></span></span></span></p>

(<a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-finnfund-partner-netwey-…; target="_blank">“Netwey”</a>), a Mexican internet service provider (ISP) founded in 2018, offering fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) and fixed broadband (HBB) connectivity. Since its inception, Netwey has experienced significant growth, reaching more than 250,000 connected homes and expanding to 17 of Mexico's 31 states. The proceeds of this investment will be used primarily to support Netwey's expansion plans, focusing on the expansion of its fiber network.</p>

<p><a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-supports-responsible-agr…; target="_blank"><span lang="EN-US">The Responsible Commodities Facility (RCF)</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> is a farmer financing program initially implemented in the 2022/2023 crops season, that promotes the responsible production and trade of Deforestation and Conversion-Free (DCF) soy in Brazil's Cerrado biome. Managed by Sustainable Investment Management Ltd. (SIM), the RCF offers lower-interest credit lines as a financial incentive to soy farmers committed to zero deforestation and no conversion of native vegetation. </span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p>&nbsp;</p><p><span lang="EN-US">For the 2025/2026 season, the RCF plans to expand the program to US$200 million. IDB Invest aims to participate in this new funding round, contributing 12.5% of the total project cost through a 1-year bullet payment investment of up to US$25 million in the senior tranche, with US$10 million committed and up to US$15 million uncommitted credit lines. </span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p>&nbsp;</p><p><span lang="EN-US">The program operates as a self-liquidating special purpose entity, providing loans to farmers for short-term crop financing. These loans are through Rural Product Certificates (CPRs) issued by farmers with pledges of crop or fiduciary liens as collateral, which serve as assets for the agribusiness receivables certificates (CRAs), like an ABS (Asset Backed Securities), issued by Opea Securitization company to fund the program. The CRAs are expected to be classified as Green Bonds.</span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p>&nbsp;</p><p><span lang="EN-US">The specific objectives of the RCF 2025-2026 expansion include supporting approximately 500 farms with crop financing to produce 640,000 tons of DCF soy. The project will also conserve about 92,000 hectares of native vegetation, with at least 5% of excess native vegetation over the minimum required by local regulations, contributing significantly to environmental preservation. Additionally, it will help conserve over 38.9 Mt of CO₂ equivalent stocks on participating farms, further enhancing the program's positive climate impact</span><span lang="PT"></span></p>

project_name: Anillo Vial Periférico: Transforming Lima's Urban Road Infrastructure
description: <p><span>The Project, which involves the construction, operation, and maintenance of a 34.8 km long, six lane, toll expressway in Lima, Peru, will also include toll-free side roads for local traffic, 4.22 km of double and triple lane tunnels, 11 viaducts, 16 underpasses, 18 overpasses, pedestrian crossings every 500 m, 3 main toll stations, and two lateral toll stations. project_name: Namu Travel: Expanding sustainable travel in LATAM
description: <p>Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Panama and Costa Rica, <a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-partners-namu-travel-str…; target="_blank">Corporación de Viajes Mundiales S.A.</a>, operating under the brand Namu Travel Group, has established itself as a leading travel company with a strong presence primarily in Central America.</p><p><br>Positioning itself as a leader in the travel sector, Namu specializes in creating tailor-made programs and itineraries that offer unique and enriching experiences for its clients, who mainly come from the United States and Europe—fostering a distinctive connection with the region.</p><p>The group has built close relationships with over a hundred suppliers, most of which are small boutique hotels, tour operators, and tourist transportation providers—many of them classified as Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs).</p><p>The transaction involves the provision of a working capital loan of up to US$9 million, with a term of up to 540 days, available over a period of 3.5 years, and renewable for an additional term. The objective is to channel funds to these SME suppliers through a pre-purchase program for hotel nights or tourism experiences, effectively improving the operating capital and cash availability of these service providers. Most of these Eligible Suppliers are classified as Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs).</p><p>In addition, a long-term credit line of up to US$3 million will be included, with a term of up to 3.5 years, renewable, aimed at financing investments in capital and technology that will support the growth and development of Namu Travel Group, enabling its expansion across Latin America and the Caribbean.</p><p>SMEs play a vital role in the tourism industry, generating a significant share of employment in the sector. However, they face various challenges that can affect their competitiveness and financial sustainability, such as limited access to financing and capital. Through Namu’s pre-purchase program, these SMEs will gain access to advance cash flows that will allow them to strengthen their financial solvency and implement necessary operational improvements—such as facility upgrades, new equipment acquisition, and employee retention during the low season—ultimately enhancing their business resilience.</p>

project_name: Routes 2 and 7 PPP additional works: enhancing road infrastructure in Paraguay
description: <p>The Ministry of Public Works and Communications of Paraguay (MOPC) has signed an addendum to the PY02 Highway concession agreement with the Special Purpose Vehicle <em>Rutas del Este</em>, made up of Sacyr Concesiones (60%) and Ocho A (40%). Through this addendum, the highway will be expanded to improve connectivity between the capital, Asunción, and <span>other parts of the country</span>, enhance safety, and promote regional development.</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>The project consists of a structuring road network, which includes key works such as the Ypacaraí–Areguá bypasses and a 3.6-kilometer elevated urban expressway with two carriageways and four lanes, connecting Ñu Guasú and Silvio Pettirossi avenues. It also includes two new connections to Route PY02 that are essential for improving connectivity. The first connection begins at kilometer 41 of Route PY02, enhancing accessibility via Ypacaraí, Patiño, Areguá, and Luque. The second connection starts at kilometer 43 and will enhance access through San Bernardino.</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>Both corridors will be part of the <em>Structuring Road Access Network</em>, which will link to Ñu Guasú and Silvio Pettirossi avenues, establishing a more efficient system for entering and exiting the metropolitan area. The proposal also includes the comprehensive operation and maintenance of the road network, ensuring its long-term functionality.</p>

project_name: SABESP: Accelerating Universal Sanitation In São Paulo With  Brazil’s First Blue A/B Structure
description: <p><span>The Project consists of a senior unsecured corporate loan to </span><a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-finances-sabesp-accelera…; target="_blank"><span>Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo</span></a><span> (“SABESP”) to fund investments needed to support the company to achieve the sewage universalization goals, expanding sewage collection, and treatment services from 85%&nbsp;to 99% of the population in the State of São Paulo, Brazil.</span></p><p><span>The loan will be labeled Blue for its investments in sustainable wastewater management and pollution prevention, listed as eligible blue project categories.</span></p>

project_name: AES Vientos Bonaerenses Wind Power Expansion Loan Bahía Blanca
description: <p><span>The Vientos Bonaerenses III and IV project (the “Project”) involves the construction of two wind farms (Vientos Bonaerenses III or “VBIII” and Vientos Bonaerenses IV or “VBIV”) in the municipalities of Tornquist (VBIII) and Bahía Blanca (VBIV), in the province of Buenos Aires.&nbsp;</span></p><p><span>The Project, which will consist of 16 wind turbines (8 per farm) and have a total installed capacity of 99.1 MW, includes the supply, installation, engineering, procurement, and construction of: i) the VBIII and VBIV wind farms; ii) an expansion of the existing 33 kV electrical substation to evacuate the energy generated to the Argentine Interconnection System (“SADI”) through the Tres Picos 132/33 kV Transformation Station; iii) an internal underground medium-voltage and communication network; iv) an operation and maintenance building; and v) access roads and auxiliary roads within the farms.</span></p>

project_name: Paraguay Route 1 Project – Mercosur Routes Consortium
description: <p><span>The Project consists of a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) contract&nbsp;for the design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of National Route No. 1 in Paraguay (the “Project”), to be awarded by the Ministry of Public Works and Communications (MOPC).&nbsp;</span></p><p><span>The Project primarily involves the expansion and modernization of approximately 108 km of existing operational road segments (brownfield), including the duplication to four lanes, as well as the construction of bridges, interchanges, and bypasses&nbsp;to divert traffic from urban areas. The PPP contract will have a 30-year term.&nbsp;</span></p><p><span>For execution and revenue calculation purposes under the contract, the Project is divided into 18 sections or functional units, each with a specific weighting.</span></p>
domicile: Avenida Aviadores del Chaco 2812, Edificio Plaza Center, Piso 7 – Asunción

project_name: Paracel: Sustainable Forestry and Competitive Infrastructure Financing
description: <p><a href="https://idbinvest.org/en/news-media/idb-invest-supports-paracel-largest…; target="_blank"><span lang="EN-US">Paracel S.A.</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> (“Paracel,” the “Company,” or the “Client”) is developing a large-scale pulp project in Concepción and Amambay, Paraguay, which includes the construction of an industrial plant for bleached eucalyptus Kraft pulp, with an annual production capacity of 1.8 million tons, a forestry program covering 203,000 hectares, and various complementary civil works, (i.e., power lines, substations, port, and access roads) the “Pulp Project”.</span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p>&nbsp;</p><p><span lang="EN-US">The Pulp Project was approved by IDB Invest in 2022, and since then, Paracel has been complying with the requirements established in both IDB Invest’s Environmental and Social Sustainability Policy and the Environmental and Social Action Plan agreed upon by the parties.</span></p>
domicile: Av. Aviadores del Chaco 2050, Asunción, Paraguay

project_name: Mexican NBFI Regulatory Enhancement Transition Bond in Mexico
description: <p><span lang="EN-US">The transaction consists of a joint securitization through the issuance of Fiduciary Securities Certificates (senior debt) for up to $1,000 million Mexican pesos, within a program of up to $2,000 million Mexican pesos, structured through an issuer trust with Banco Multiva as trustee, and backed by productive credit portfolios originated by Multiple Purpose Financial Companies (“SOFOMs”), AFIX, ATREVUS, COFINE, FTV and Grupo KELQ. The issuance will have a term of up to 6 years, with 18 months of revolving period, subsequent full-turbo amortization. The structure incorporates multi-originator diversification, interest rate hedging and a partial financial guarantee from FIRA and NAFIN for up to 18% each, which allows achieving a AAA local target rating. The resources will be allocated to finance and refinance productive credits to MSMEs, under a social label issuance, with the objective of improving access to long-term funding for SOFOMs in the productive sector, reducing financial costs and strengthening financial inclusion and economic development.&nbsp;</span></p>

project_name: Iguá Sergipe: Universalization And Modernization Of Water And Sanitation Services
description: <p>The Project involves the construction, operation, and maintenance of water distribution and sewage collection and treatment services across 74 municipalities in the state of Sergipe, Brazil, directly benefiting approximately 2.3 million people. The Project is governed by a 35‑year concession agreement granted to Iguá Sergipe S.A.</p><p>Total capital expenditures are estimated at approximately R$6 billion through 2033, allocated to water supply and sanitation investments. Water-related capex will focus on expanding and rehabilitating distribution networks and replacing water meters as part of a water‑loss reduction program. Sanitation investments will include the development of new sewage collection networks and interceptors, the construction of new wastewater treatment plants, and the installation of new sewage pumping stations.</p>

client_name: Sacos de Polipropileno Especializados, S.A. de C.V.
description: <p><span>The APP La Dorada – Chiriguaná Railway Corridor is a strategic initiative led by the National Infrastructure Agency (ANI) to reactivate freight rail transport in Colombia, promoting intermodality and logistical efficiency. The project involves the construction, rehabilitation, improvement, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of a railway corridor of approximately 525 kilometers, connecting the municipalities of La Dorada (Caldas) and Chiriguaná (Cesar), and crossing five departments and twenty-five municipalities. It also includes the modernization of administrative and operational infrastructure, such as control buildings, workshops, communication and signaling systems, as well as the construction of logistics centers for cargo transfer.</span></p><p><span>The scope of the project covers three main functional units: (1) the rehabilitation and operation of the railway corridor and its branches, (2) the construction and operation of administrative and operational control infrastructure, and (3) the logistics infrastructure for cargo transfer services. The project aims to strengthen connectivity between the country’s center and the Caribbean coast, boost foreign trade, energize local economies, and improve road and pedestrian safety in the areas of influence. It also encourages the hiring of local labor, the participation of regional suppliers, and the improvement of educational infrastructure, contributing to environmental sustainability through the reduction of CO₂ emissions and efficient resource use.</span></p>

project_name: Corporación Favorita: Promoting sustainable investment in Panama
description: <p>Corporación Favorita is a leading retail conglomerate in Ecuador and the country’s largest supermarket operator, with a diversified portfolio that includes supermarket formats, wholesale operations, and e-commerce. It operates in Panama through its subsidiary Rey Holding Corp, as well as in other Latin American countries.</p><p>The proposed financing includes a package of up to US$58 million, with a tenor of up to 5 years, structured to support strategic growth and sustainability initiatives focused on the Group’s operations in Panama. It comprises: (i) a committed secured senior loan of up to US$30 million, provided by IDB Invest and mobilization resources, primarily intended to finance the expansion of the Distribution Center in Panama and, to a lesser extent, the refinancing of medium-term debt to extend maturities; (ii) a secured senior loan of up to US$3 million with concessional resources, aimed at implementing a pilot battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Panama, potentially the first at industrial scale; and (iii) an uncommitted secured senior loan of up to US$25 million, which may be used to finance future growth and investment needs in Panama or Ecuador.</p><p>&nbsp;</p>
domicile: Av. General Enríquez vía Cotogchoa, Quito, Ecuador

project_name: Club Atletico River Plate: Investing in Sports Facilities for Social Inclusion

Banco Industrial, S.A. is one of the largest banks in Guatemala, operating a full service universal bank model. The customer segments enterprises and retail clients are approximately equal in size.

The Mauritius Commercial Bank Ltd (MCB) operates as a leading integrated financial services provider headquartered in Mauritius, offering retail, corporate, wealth management, and non‑banking financial services such as leasing, factoring, asset management, and capital markets across the Indian Ocean region and select African and global markets.

The business model centers on deploying financial, human, intellectual, manufactured, natural, and social capital to deliver tailored financing products, investment and advisory services, and digital banking solutions that both drive stakeholder value and support sustainable regional economic growth.

MCB distributes its services through a mix of physical branches, ATMs, and robust digital platforms in Mauritius, complemented by subsidiaries in the Indian Ocean region and representative offices in Africa, Europe, and the Middle East. Liquid Group – a technology and digital solutions provider with operations in more than 25 countries primarily in Eastern, Southern and Central Africa - was incorporated in 2007 and has since then built and operated the largest multi-country, open access fibre network in Africa with an extension of more than 110,000km. 
The company’s network is available to a broad range of customers. The client portfolio consists of more than 11,700 corporate clients and more than 137,000 small and medium sized companies and individual customers. In addition, Liquid sells a number of services to leverage its fibre infrastructure, e.g. internet access, cloud solutions, cybersecurity and others.

JSC Bank of Georgia (“the bank”) is one of the largest universal banks in Georgia. As a systemically important bank with a significant digital presence, JSC Bank of Georgia serves over 2 million monthly active retail customers and more than 129,000 monthly active business clients (as at Q1 2026). The bank was founded in 1994 in Tbilisi, following the privatization of a state-owned bank.

client_name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria Colombia S.A.
description: BBVA Colombia S.A. is a systemically relevant universal bank and the 4th largest market player in Colombia. It is part of Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria S.A. (BBVA) group, one of the largest financial groups worldwide, headquartered in Spain.

Adenia Entrepreneurial Fund (I) LP (AEF I), is a fund managed by Adenia Capital founded in 2002. AEF I is the sixth fund of Adenia Capital. It marks a strategic expansion of the manager. The fund is focused on control investments in lower mid-cap companies in Africa. The manager has an on-the-ground presence in eight key markets in Africa (Kenya, Madagascar, Ghana, Cote d’Ivoire, South Africa, Nigeria, Morocco and Mauritius).

Gulf Renewable Energy Company Limited (GRE) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Gulf Development Public Company Limited (Gulf). Established in 2018 as Gulf’s renewable energy investment arm, GRE has a total committed capacity of 5,461.2 MW, of which 1,355.5 MW is currently in operation. The proposed transaction is backed by an unconditional and irrevocable first-demand guarantee from Gulf.

Gulf Development Public Company Limited (Gulf) was founded in 2007, Gulf is a leading power generation company in Thailand, holding the largest portfolio of contracted power purchase agreements (PPAs) in the country. As of November 2023, GED has a total installed capacity of 12,405 MW.

JSCB TBC Bank (“TBCUZ”) is a relatively new player in Uzbekistan’s banking sector, having reached break-even in 2023. A key differentiator of TBCUZ is its fully digital banking model, which provides clients with fast, efficient, and seamless financial services. This innovative approach enhances financial accessibility for borrowers, positioning TBCUZ as a forward-thinking institution in Uzbekistan’s evolving financial landscape.

DEG provides a loan of EUR 50 million with a maturity of 5 years to support INPASA’s expansion of corn‑based ethanol production in Brazil.  INPASA is Brazil’s largest ethanol producer, accounting for roughly 10% of total ethanol output and close to 50% of the country’s corn‑ethanol production, operating a rapidly growing portfolio of modern, high‑efficiency plants.  The company demonstrates strong profitability, robust cash generation, and a strategic advantage due to its location in major corn‑producing regions and its ability to run year‑round production.

Ferretería EPA S.A. de C.V. (“EPA El Salvador”) is the sister company of DEG’s long‑standing client Ferretería EPA S.A. (“EPA Costa Rica”). The company operates Home Improvement and Do‑It‑Yourself (HIDIY) retail stores in Costa Rica, Guatemala, El Salvador and Venezuela, where it consistently ranks among the top three players in each market.

Bandwidth and Cloud Services (“BCS”) is a midsize wholesale telecom service provider established in 2009 and operating in southern, central and east Africa. The group owns and operates ~13,000km of physical backbone fibre infrastructure spanning DRC, Uganda, Rwanda, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Angola under respective long-term licenses. The group’s national subsidiaries provide mainly wholesale telecom infrastructure operations on the BCS fibre network to Mobile Network Operators, Internet Service Providers and content providers.

The E2VC III Fund is focusing on seed and early growth investments into internationally scalable tech business models. The fund is managed by E2VC III B.V, an Istanbul based early growth fund manager domiciled in the Netherlands.

(“ReNew Global”).

Goutougo is a project company established with the purpose of developing, constructing and operating a 50MW solar PV plant in Côte d’Ivoire. 
The project shareholder is Dubai based Amea Power Ltd., one of the fastest growing renewable energy devel-opers with increasing experience in Africa.

CTG Control is a project company established for the development, construction and operation of a 2,851 km fiber‑optic cable route and related infrastructure connecting Querétaro, Mexico, with Phoenix, USA. The project forms part of the C3ntro Telecom group, an established telecom carrier with three decades of experience providing voice, SMS, data and fiber services across Mexico.

client_name: VIVRITI FIXED INCOME FUND SERIES 3 IFSC LLP
description: VIVRITI FIXED INCOME FUND SERIES 3 IFSC LLP (VIRAF) is a close-ended fund set up in March 2023 in the form of a Limited Liability Partnership domiciled in GIFT City. The Fund will be predominantly providing debt financing to Non‑Bank Financial Institutions by investing in asset‑backed securities (ABS) issued by these insti-tutions. A holder of senior debt in VIRAF would be seen as lending to a corporate entity, making the senior debt a corporate exposure to VIRAF rather than a securitization position.

client_name: Banco para la Comercialización y la Producción S.A.
description: Banco para la Comercialización y la Producción S.A. (BANCOP) is the first cooperative-owned bank in Paraguay. Founded in 2012, it operates under a universal banking license, providing funding with a focus on agricultural, livestock and industrial activities.

client_name: Lendable MSME FinTech Credit Fund II SCSp, SICAV-RAIF
description: Lendable MSME FinTech Credit Fund II SCSp, SICAV-RAIF (LMFCF II) is a USD 250 million structured debt fund launched in 2025 that provides senior secured financing to leading fintech lenders and digital finance platforms serving MSMEs across emerging markets. The fund focuses on tech-enabled MSME lenders, asset-finance providers and embedded-finance platforms. LMFCF II is managed by Royalton Partners as AIFM, with Lendable acting as investment advisor. Since 2016, Lendable has deployed over USD 804 million across fintech lenders in emerging market countries.

Denizbank A.Ş. (“Denizbank”), established in 1997, is a medium‑sized privately owned bank and ranks ninth among Turkish banks with total assets of around EUR 40.5 bn as of September 2025. The bank operates across a broad range of customer segments—including retail, private banking, SMEs, corporates, agriculture, trade finance as well as public and project finance—and benefits from a well‑established franchise network in Türkiye, a strong brand and a loyal customer base. 

DFS is the Special Purpose Company (SPC) created as the issuer of notes under Denizbank’s Diversified Payment Rights (DPR) Program.

JSC TBC Bank (“TBC”) is a long-standing and trusted partner of DEG. It was founded in 1992 as a universal bank by two Georgian entrepreneurial families and has since then become the largest bank in Georgia with a market share of approx. 40% in customer loans and deposits. TBC is a systemically important bank and is active in all business segments. The bank is the market leader in the retail segment and the leading partner bank for MSMEs offering them also extensive business support programs.

The Reforestation Fund I (TRF I), established in 2022, is a private equity timberland fund focusing on the ac-quisition of degraded land and the subsequent establishment of sustainably managed greenfield commercial tree farms on ~50% of the portfolio, and restoration of native forests and ecosystems on ~50% of the portfo-lio. The Fund targets the generation of high-quality forest carbon credits from both the restored areas and commercial tree farms. The Fund will invest in Brazil (≥ 50%) and Uruguay as well as potentially in other Latin American countries.
The fund will be managed by BTG Pactual Timberland Investment Group, LLC (“TIG”), part of the asset management vertical of Banco BTG Pactual S.A., a publicly listed Brazilian financial company.

client_name: Axian Telecom Holding and Management Ltd
description: Axian Telecom Holding and Management Ltd UAE (AT) is a mediumsized, integrated mobile network operator with a strong market position in niche markets. It is part of a family-owned Malagasy conglomerate, which is active in different sectors on the African continent. AT consists of three business segments: mobile/fixed network operators, digital infrastructure (towercos, fiber, data centers), and mobile financial services. The Group started operations in Madagascar and then subsequently widened its presence to Mayotte/Reunion, the Comoros, Senegal, Togo, and Tanzania, and recently founded new tower companies in the DRC and Uganda.

Banga Building Materials Limited (“BANGA”, “Company”), founded in Bangladesh in 2007, manufactures a broad range of building-material and household products, including PVC pipes, doors, bathroom fittings, elec-trical switches, energy‑saving bulbs, kitchenware, and stationery. The company is part of the family-owned PRAN-RFL Group, a major food-processing and plastics manufacturer in Bangladesh.
BANGA operates a nationwide distribution network with approximately 8,500 dealers, including 2,500 dealers that exclusively sell BANGA products.. While the majority of sales are domestic, BANGA also exports to around 20 countries across Asia, Africa, Europe, USA and Oceania. Since 2013, BANGA has been a reliable client of DEG.

client_name: Regional MSME Investment Fund for Sub-Saharan Africa S.A., SICAV-SIF

REGMIFA is a debt fund with a regional focus on Sub-Saharan Africa, which provides predominantly local currency senior loans to microfinance institutions, local commercial banks and other financial institutions, including fintech companies. The Fund was set up in 2010 by KfW on behalf of the BMZ.
REGMIFA is managed by Symbiotics Asset Management S.A., a Switzerland-based asset manager and advi-sor. It is part of the Symbiotics group which was founded in 2004 and is active in the field of impact investment.

Banco Múltiple BHD, S.A. is a commercial bank incorporated in the Dominican Republic and ranks among the top three banks in the country. The bank is a market leader in MSME finance and has a strong footprint in gender-focused lending.

Its business model centers on providing financial services to retail and corporate clients, with a strategic focus on underserved segments. BHD operates nationwide through a broad branch network and digital channels.

client_name: Asociación de Cooperativas Argentinas C. L.
description:

The organization maintains a presence across 12 provinces in Argentina, with its strongest footprint in Buenos Aires, Santa Fe, Córdoba and Entre Ríos.

Banco Continental is the largest universal bank in Paraguay, operating since the 1980’s and the only one with investment grade, with a strong focus in corporate banking.
As Paraguay’s largest bank, Banco Continental plays a key role in supporting the country’s economic growth and employs around 1,400 staff members. The bank is recognized as a pioneer in sustainability topics in the Paraguayan financial sector and in the use of technology and digitalization for both business and market inno-vation. Furthermore, through Fundación Continental, the Bank shows its commitment to fostering community development.

The comprehensive product portfolio of natural ingredients ranges from natural flavours, colours, health ingredients, a broad range of plant-based ingredients to ingredient systems and end-to-end solutions.

The bank is part of the regional group Promérica Financial Corporation. It is the fourth largest private bank in Costa Rica in terms of assets, as of year-end 2024.

client_name: Banco Promerica de Costa Rica, S.A.
description: Banco Promérica de Costa Rica, S.A. (BPCR), established in 1992, is a Costa Rica-based bank, that provides financial services to individuals and companies. The bank is part of the regional group Promérica Financial Corporation. It is the fourth largest private bank in Costa Rica in terms of assets, as of year-end 2024.

The German family owned business Selecta one is one of the leading global floriculture breeders, selling flower and plant starting material as well as IP licenses. Established more than 90 years ago, the group has over 60 years of breeding experience. Today, Selecta is the global top-3 player in floriculture breeding with worldwide market leadership in key products carnation and poinsettia.

FirstRand Bank is one of the leading financial institutions in South Africa. It has three separately branded divisions in South Africa: First National Bank for retail and commercial banking, Rand Merchant Bank for corporate and investment banking, and WesBank, the largest vehicle finance provider in the country.

‘Abydos for Renewable Energy’ is a project company incorporated to design, build and operate a 1000 MWac Solar PV power plant with 600 MWh of battery storage in the Aswan governorate of Egypt. 

Main sponsor of the project company is AMEA Power (UAE), with a participation of 60%. AMEA Power is an existing KfW-DEG client with a positive track-record. The other sponsor is Kyuden International Corporation (40%), a strategic financial investor belonging to the stock listed Kyushu Electric Power Co. Inc, a Japan-based utility company providing integrated energy services.

DEG will invest USD 10m in the Brazilian company Combio Energia S.A., that supplies renewable thermal energy to the industry from biomass and renewable electricity with projects in several regions of Brazil, serving a wide range of customers in the mining, pulp and paper, biofuels, food and beverage segments, among others.

CrossBoundary Energy Holdings (CBEH) is a leading developer, owner, and operator of renewable energy solutions for commercial and industrial (C&I) clients across Africa. Through its local subsidiaries, the company provides both grid‑tied and captive IPP models tailored to the needs of corporate customers. Since its incep-tion in 2015, CBEH has built up a portfolio comprising more than 28 operational assets totaling 62 MW of installed capacity and 30 MWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) across 10 African countries. Further nine projects with an expected capacity of approximately 255 MW are currently under construction.

Endiya III fund targets Indian early-stage tech companies developing globally applicable products. Endiya concentrates on B2B business models across Digital Health & Life Sciences, Enterprise Digital Adoption, Digital Industry & Intelligent Mobility and FinTech. Product development of target firms is located in India benefiting from domestic engineering and software develop­ment ecosystem and labor cost differential offering international competitive advantages to scale investees. 

The fund is managed by Endiya iKsana Advisory Services LLP (“Endiya” or the “Manager”), established in 2016, an India focused fund manager who specializes in early-stage investments (Seed to Series B).

The manager is operating two predecessor funds with a total Assets under Management of USD 87m based on a similar investment strategy.

The customer of the Payita project is LCV Ecoener Solares Dominicana, which is owned by Ecoener, a Span-ish independent power producer (IPP) specializing in renewable energy.

Ecoener has currently 427 MW within 41 projects (mainly photovoltaic, but also wind and hydro energy) under operation. Another 360 MW are under construction and up to 1357 MW are at different development stages. Ecoener’s strategy is to continue growing in markets with energy imbalances, Power Purchase agreements denominated in hard currencies, deep debt markets, good transmission networks and fiscal incentives that support the development of renewable energies. Ecoener brings extensive experience in the Dominican Re-public through its Cumayasa I and II projects (96.5 MW), both fully developed and constructed by the compa-ny and now successfully in operation.
The company has been listed on the Spanish stock exchange since 2021 and is majority-owned by its founder and president, a Spanish entrepreneur with over 30 years of experience in renewable energy.

Armeconombank is a mid-sized universal bank, ranking 7th in Armenia by total assets, with a strong focus on lending to local micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), alongside a diverse range of retail and corporate banking services. The bank provides financial products such as loans, deposits, trade finance, and payment solutions, catering to a broad customer base.
AEB operates an extensive distribution network with 54 branches across all regions of Armenia and a work-force of approximately 900 employees (as of Dec. 2024)

China Water Affairs Group Ltd. is the Hong Kong-listed (HKEX) holding company of a group of companies, which own and operate all services in the water supply and wastewater treatment sector. The group is active in 24 Chinese provinces with more than 100 cities/counties, servicing more than 30 million people.

JC Growth Credit Fund 1 LP (the “Fund”) is a newly set up structured fund to provide venture debt to growth-stage technology companies in Southeast Asia. Venture Debt a relatively new financing option in the region providing growth-stage companies with additional funding.
CHG-MERIDIAN México is an asset solution provider offering efficient technology solutions to companies investing in IT, material handling equipment, industrial equipment, health care and fleet.

client_name: Banco de América Central Honduras, S.A.
description:
Banco de América Central Honduras, S.A. is the third largest bank in Honduras and is part of the Central American BAC Credomatic Group. 

Founded in Nicaragua in 1952, the BAC Credomatic brand has grown to become one of the largest financial services groups in Central America. The bank is successful with a customer-centric product offering and client interface and pursues a dedicated sustainability strategy (triple positive value). Other members of the BAC Group are also clients of DEG.

Rönesans Holding is a multinational construction and investment company founded in 1993 in Turkey. Its business model centers on creating sustainable value through construction, real estate, energy, healthcare, and industrial investments, reinvesting profits into long-term assets and strategic partnerships. The company operates globally, with core markets in Turkey and the Netherlands and projects in 31 countries.
With over 34,000 employees across 31 countries, Rönesans Holding promotes fair labor practices, zero toler-ance for child/forced labor, and implements inclusive HR policies. With 85% of its workforce hired locally and a strong commitment to local procurement, Rönesans actively supports economic development in the region where it operates.

client_name: Thanh Thanh Cong Bien Hoa Joint Stock Company
description: Thanh Thanh Cong Bien Hoa Joint Stock Company (TTCBH) established in year 1995 is the leading sugar producer in Vietnam. The company is a fully integrated player who covers the whole value chain from the plantation of sugar cane to the refining of sugar and the production of value-added consumer goods. Its main business area is the production and distribution of refined sugar.

SchneiTec Beyond Co., Ltd. has been established to construct, operate and maintain a greenfield 150MW solar PV power plant located in Pursat Province, Cambodia. Project sponsor is SchneiTec Company Ltd., the leading IPP in Cambodia. More than 450MW solar PV utility-scale power plants have been constructed and are currently being operated by the company.

Taaleem Management Services is a leading higher education provider in Egypt, with a strategic focus on medical and health-related academic programs. Established in 2015, Taaleem operates two fully licensed universities in Upper Egypt and West Cairo, a third is under construction in East Cairo. The company addresses the growing demand for high quality, affordable education among Egypt’s middle class. As of the academic year 2024/2025, Taaleem enrolled over 12,000 students across 14 faculties.

client_name: Somerset Indus Healthcare India Fund III
description: Somerset Healthcare Investment Advisors III Pvt Ltd is an independent fund manager focused on India. The company targets small to mid size healthcare businesses across various subsectors. Since mid-2024, Somerset has been raising capital for its third fund, Somerset III.

Global Gender Smart Fund S.A. (GGSF, formerly known as MEF) is a globally acting evergreen blended finance debt fund, which was initiated in 2009 by KfW on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic and IFC. It aims to strengthen the provision of gender-smart and responsible financial services to underserved women, women-owned or women-led businesses in developing markets, with the aim to improve livelihoods, increase gender balance and outreach, and promote women’s leadership.
GGSF is managed by Innpact Fund Management S.A., a Luxembourg-based impact management platform.

client_name: Klar Technologies, S.A. de C.V., S.F.P.
description: Klar Technologies established in 2019 is a digital bank operating in Mexico. Klar provides a comprehensive, fully digital and app-based platform for financial services. Klar prioritizes technological innovation to facilitate seamless integration of individuals into the financial market. The fintech company offers its customers access to payment solutions, deposit services, and lending opportunities. The company maintains an office in Berlin, which serves as the base for the platform's developers.

client_name: La Cooperativa de Productores de Leche Dos Pinos R.L.
description: Established in 1947, Dos Pinos is the biggest dairy company in Costa Rica and among the largest agribusinesses in Central America. As a cooperative, it is owned by more than 1,800 associated farmers and workers. Dos Pinos purchases the raw milk from its members, processes it and distributes a complete range of dairy products. In addition, Dos Pinos sells other food and beverages under its own brands and provides agricultural inputs and services to its associates.

St. Georges Bank is a mid-sized Panamanian commercial bank founded in 2001. Its loan portfolio focuses on commercial and SME customers, both locally and throughout the Central American region. St. Georges belongs to Promerica Group, with presence in Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Dominican Republic, Ecuador and the Cayman Islands.

JSC Coca-Cola Bottlers Georgia (CCBG) was founded in 1993 and is the bottler and distributor of carbonated drinks, juices, cold tea, mineral water and energy drinks. Exclusively licensed by The Coca-Cola Company for Coca-Cola products in Georgia and – for some products – also in Azerbaijan and Armenia. It has a strong market position (40%) and is one of the top-tier corporates in the country.

client_name: Društvo za trgovija na malo Lidl Severna Makedonija Dooel
description: Društvo za trgovija na malo Lidl Severna Makedonija Dooel (Lidl North Macedonia) is part of the Schwarz-Group, a food retailer, founded in 1973 in Germany. It is currently setting up its business in North Macedonia. Schwarz-Group is one of the biggest food retailers in the world and operates under the brands Kaufland (supermarket) and Lidl (discounter) in 27 countries in Europe as well as the USA.

client_name: Axian Telecom Holding and Management Ltd
description: Axian Telecom Holding and Management Ltd UAE, (AT), is a medium-sized, integrated and innovative mobile network operator with strong market position in niche markets. It is part of a family-owned Malagasy conglomerate, which is active in different sectors on the African continent. AT consists of three business segments: Mobile/fixed network operators, digital infrastructure (towercos, fiber, data centers), and mobile financial services. The Group started operations in Madagascar and then subsequently widened its presence to Mayotte/Reunion, the Comoros, Senegal, Togo, and Tanzania, and recently founded new tower companies in the DRC and Uganda.

client_name: Vinte Viviendas Integrales, S.A.B. DE C.V.
description: Founded in 2001, Vinte is a fully integrated homebuilder engaged in the design, development, construction, commercialization and delivery of affordable entry-level, middle-class and upper-income housing developments in Mexico. Vinte promotes EDGE certified housing by using sustainable building materials and efficient energy and water consumption. Based in Mexico City, the company has presence in six states across Mexico. By the acquisition of Servicios Corporativos Javer, S.A.B. de C.V. –  one of the biggest real estate developers in Mexico –Vinte will significantly increase its regional presence and enlarge its low-income housing portfolio.

Tiga Beruang Kalifornia Pte Ltd (“Waresix” or the “company”) is Indonesia’s largest tech-enabled multi-modal logistics platform with ambition to leverage on current inefficiencies in one of the most complex logistics markets globally.

client_name: Banco de la Producción S.A. Produbanco
description: Produbanco is a universal bank formed through the 2014 merger of Produbanco and Promerica Ecuador. It is part of the regional banking group Promerica, which operates in seven Central American countries — Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and the Dominican Republic — as well as in Ecuador and the Cayman Islands. Promerica is the largest regional banking group of its kind not affiliated with an international bank.

Access Bank Plc is a banking group headquartered in Lagos/Nigeria, serving around 61m customers across Africa, Europe, and Asia. Per December 2024 Access Bank Plc operates 14 subsidiaries across Sub-Sahara Africa, one subsidiary in the UK, and representations in six more countries.

ECOM Agroindustrial Corporation Ltd. (ECOM) is a family-owned, integrated supply chain company with operations in 40 countries. The group holds leading global market positions in coffee, cocoa, and cotton trading. Headquartered in Switzerland, ECOM serves as the group holding company and builds on a 175-year history in the agricultural commodities sector.

The company has a long-standing commitment to sustainability and has made progress in strengthening its environmental and social (E&S) management systems. ECOM has set climate targets, with a focus on deforestation mitigation and enhancing farmer resilience to climate change.

client_name: Fraport TAV Antalya Yatirim Yapim Ve Isletme AS, Turkey
description: Fraport TAV Antalya Yatırım Yapım ve İşletme A.Ş. is a special purpose vehicle established in Turkey for the purpose of operating and expanding Antalya Airport under a long-term concession. It is a joint venture between Fraport AG (Germany) and TAV Airports Holding (Turkey). The company focuses on airport operations and infrastructure development, serving as a key international aviation hub on the Turkish Riviera.
Canary IV, L.P. is a Brazil-based venture capital fund founded in 2024, focused on tech-driven and tech-enabled businesses across Latin America, with a strong emphasis on the Brazilian market.

PI Fund V (Ontario), L.P., focuses on equity investments in infrastructure, including renewable energy infrastructure, logistics & transportation (incl. electric mobility), data centers, water sewage, desalination and waste management in Latin America, and is managed by PI General Partner V Ltd. (PATRIA) - a leading alternative investment firm in Latin America.

CRDB Bank Plc is an integrated financial services provider listed on the Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange. Established in 1996, it is one of the largest banks in Tanzania. The bank offers banking services to retail, MSME, and corporate clients. It also operates two subsidiaries: CRDB Bank Burundi S.A. and CRDB Insurance Broker Ltd.

CRDB Bank Plc is an integrated financial services provider listed on the Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange. Established in 1996, it is one of the largest banks in Tanzania. The bank offers banking services to retail, MSME, and corporate clients. It also operates two subsidiaries: CRDB Bank Burundi S.A. and CRDB Insurance Broker Ltd.

Bank One is a medium-sized commercial bank in Mauritius. The bank provides a comprehensive range of retail, commercial and corporate banking services in Mauritius. Bank One provides loans to private companies across the African continent. It is a joint venture by the Kenya based Banking Group I&M Group Plc and CIEL Finance Limited which is part of one of the largest conglomerates in Mauritius.

Terabank is a mid-sized bank in Georgia, providing financial services to retail, SME and corporate clients. The bank was established in 2007, and operates since 2016 under the name Terabank.

Terabank specializes in financing small and medium-sized enterprises. It operates through a network of 32 branches across Georgia.

PT Indo ACWA Tenaga Saguling is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) established with the purpose of developing, constructing and operating a 60 MW floating solar PV plant on the Saguling dam (Java) in Indonesia. The project shareholders are ACWA Power Company and PT PLN Indonesia Power Renewables, subsidiary of PT PLN Indonesia Power, owned by Indonesian state-owned utility PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (“PLN”).

The Facility for Energy Inclusion (FEI) is a debt fund established in 2019 designed to support small-scale in-dependent power producers delivering power to the grid, mini-grids, commercial and industrial and captive power projects. FEI is managed by Cygnum Capital, an investment bank and asset manager with over USD1.1 billion in assets under management.

Viru S.A. is a leading company in the Peruvian agribusiness sector offering fresh, canned and frozen products to the global markets. The company is part of Viru Group which also has operations in US and EU.

Established in 1931, Acciona S.A. has become a leading Spanish energy and infrastructure group with almost 58,000 employees and is active in over 40 countries. Acciona S.A. takes a planning-construction-operation life-cycle approach and has become a global leader in sustainability and innovation in sectors such as renewable energy (one of the world’s largest renewable companies), transport (over 100 projects between ports, airports, and urban transport projects) and water (over 90 desalination plants, serving over 140 million people). The company’s regional focus is on Spain as well as Latin America and Australia.

Suez Wind Energy S.A.E. is a project company to design, build and operate a 1.1 GW wind farm on two sites at the coast of the Gulf of Suez in Egypt.

The project shareholders are ACWA Power and Hau Energy.

Founded in 2011, Mediterra Capital Management Ltd. is one of the leading private equity firms focusing on investments in mid-market companies and SMEs in Turkey. To date, Mediterra Capital Management Ltd. has successfully raised two funds invested across 16 investments.

DEG has already invested in the predecessor fund Mediterra Capital Partners I, LP in 2011 and continues the partnership after many years of successful cooperation by investing in the most recent fund Mediterra Capital Partners III, LP.

Revo Capital Fund III C.V. (“Revo”) is a Private Equity fund targeting investments in tech companies in the early growth stage. The fund is domiciled in the Netherlands and focuses on the Turkish and CEE market. The team is based in Istanbul. Revo is an independent Fund Manager operating since 2013.

Amethis Fund III S.C.A., SICAV-RAIF (“Amethis3”) was established in 2023 and is the third pan-African general-ist mid-cap fund managed by entities of Amethis Group  S.A. (“Amethis”) that was founded in 2012. The fund manager is headquartered in Paris, France, with fund management operations regulated in Luxembourg and four strong local African offices in Morocco, Egypt, Côte d’Ivoire and Kenya.

Biomass Energy, S.A. (“BIOMASS”) is a fully-owned subsidiary of Ingenio Magdalena S. A. (“IMSA”). IMSA is the largest sugar mill in Guatemala and operative holding company of the IMSA group. BIOMASS produces energy from IMSA’s sugarcane/bagasse, which accounts for approximately 25% of IMSA’s revenues, by selling energy to the Guatemalan energy market. IMSA has already been a client of DEG since 2016.

Valency is an agro commodity trader with increasing focus in value-chain management and expanding processing capacities to capture higher margins. Core business includes origination, processing and trading of agro commodities, mainly raw cashew nuts and cashew kernel but also sesame, soybean, grains, sugar, rice, cacao, maize, pulses and agrochemicals (e.g. fertilizers). Valency International Singapore is the holding company with operative activities; Valency International DMCC is developing to be the future operation and treasury center; the current processing capacities are mainly located in Nigeria; beyond that, Valency has market operations spread over 40 countries worldwide.

Founded in 2016, Neon Payments Ltd. (“Neon”) is a leading Brazilian neobank offering digital-only retail banking products, including credit cards, personal and payroll loans. Focused on Brazil’s low-income population, Neon aims to improve financial access with simple and transparent solutions for the underbanked. While the UK-based Holding is non-operative, all business activities are exclusively focused on the Brazilian market through the company’s regulated subsidiaries.

Eco-Business Sub-Fund II is an open ended, structured debt fund founded in 2019 providing loans to sustainable agriculture/ agri-processing, fishery/ aquaculture, forestry and tourism in Sub-Saharan Africa. Fund Manager is Finance in Motion, a well-known partner for DEG and KfW.

MC IV is the fourth Private Equity Fund managed by Mediterrania Capital Partners Ltd. The Manager is head-quartered in Malta and operates offices in Egypt, Morocco, Côte d’Ivoire and Mauritius. MC IV will continue to follow the predecessor funds’ strategy as a sector agnostic PE fund investing in North Africa and francophone West Africa.

client_name: Latin American Green Bond Fund S.A. SICAV-SIF
description: The Latin America Green Bond Fund (LAGREEN) is an open ended, structured debt fund focusing on investments in green and social bonds in Latin America. It was launched in 2019 with KfW acting as anchor investor on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the European Union. LAGREEN is advised by experienced, Frankfurt am Main based asset manager Finance in Motion (FIM). As the fund has been launched in 2019, portfolio as well as funding are still building up and the fund has not yet reached its target volume (USD 500m by 2028).

JK Tyre was incorporated in 1951 as a private limited company and converted into a public limited company in 1974 listed at Mumbai stock exchanges. JK Tyre produces all sorts of tires ranging from Truck/Bus, passenger car, motor cycle, three-wheeler and off road tires. In 1977, the company started with a capacity of 0.5 million tires per annum and now has a combined capacity of over 34 million tires per annum in its 12 plants- 9 in India and 3 in Mexico.

JK Tyre has a significant global presence and is present in around 100 countries with over 230 global distributors. The company also has an extensive retail and distribution network of over 6000 dealers and 700 dedicated brand shops called Steel Wheels and Xpress Wheels. Nevertheless, the majority of its income is generated in India. In FY23-24, exports represented 12% of total sales.

Ingenio Magdalena S.A. (IMSA), incorporated in 1974 in Guatemala, is the largest sugar producer in the country representing approximately 25% of the local market share and operative holding company of the IMSA Group. More than half of the group’s revenues are generated by exports.

Casa Elvira, S.A is a subsidiary of Ingenio Magdalena S.A. (IMSA), which will hold the new sugar mill financed by DEG. Casa Elvira, S.A. acts as a co-Borrower for this transaction. IMSA, incorporated in 1974 in Guatemala, is the largest sugar producer in the country (representing approximately 25% of the local market share) and operative holding company of the IMSA Group. More than half of the group’s revenues are generated by ex-ports.

YOKO, established by GreenYellow, is a diversified commercial and industrial (C&I) solar buy-and-build plat-form operating in Thailand and Vietnam. It consolidates various project companies in the region, holding an initial capacity of approximately 189 MW. YOKO’s portfolio primarily consists of rooftop solar projects, complemented by floating solar installations. GreenYellow, the developer and majority owner of YOKO, is a globally active French company focused on decarbonization, with a total installed or under-construction capacity of 1.3 GWp.

Finanzauto S.A. BIC provides financing to retail and commercial (micro and SME) clients for the purchase of vehicles. The company was founded in 1970 and is one of the largest non-banking financial institutions in its segment in Colombia.

NSIA Banque Côte d’Ivoire is a well-established bank set up in 1906 by the Belgian “Belgolaise” which used to be a subsidiary of Fortis Bank. 

In 2006 the Bank was acquired by NSIA Group which is a pan-African business group with operations in 12 West and Central African countries active in banking & finance (4 banks and 1 stocks brokerage firm), insurance (20 insurance companies), technology and real estate. 

NSIA is one of the leading universal banks in Côte d’Ivoire and the only Ivorian owned Tier I bank.

Naked Financial Technology Pty Ltd., established 2016, is a leading full-stack InsurTech player in South Africa offering personal-line car, home and single item insurance. Naked’s operation is based 100% on technology, as pricing, underwriting, claims management are all algorithm-driven, which translates into better customer experience and higher operation efficiency compared to traditional insurance companies.
CHGMex is an asset solution provider offering efficient technology solutions to companies investing in IT, material handling equipment, industrial equipment, health care and fleet.

client_name: Društvo za trgovija na malo LIDL SEVERNA MAKEDONIJA DOOEL
description: Društvo za trgovija na malo LIDL SEVERNA MAKEDONIJA DOOEL (Lidl North Macedonia) is part of the Schwarz-Group, a food retailer, founded in 1973 in Germany. It is currently setting up its business in North Macedonia. Schwarz-Group is one of the biggest food retailers in the world and operates under the brands Kaufland (supermarket) and Lidl (discounter) in 27 countries in Europe as well as the USA.

ETC Group (ETG) is a large and diversified conglomerate and supply chain manager with a significant footprint in Africa. Established in 1967 in Kenya the group owns and operates a vertically integrated supply chain, covering procurement, processing, warehousing and distribution. ETG manages over 460 warehouses and operates more than 120 processing plants across its extensive network.

New Energy Africa (NEA) Kolda S.A. is a project company established with the purpose of developing, constructing and operating a 60 MW solar photovoltaic (PV) plant and 20 MW / 72 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS).

The project shareholder is Axian Energy, part of Axian Group, a pan-African group that operates in 15 countries and specializes in five industries with high growth potential: telecoms, energy, financial services, real estate and open innovation. Aixan Group is a signatory of the UN Global Compact initiative and committed to the integration of its 10 principles into its policies and operations.

Productos Nevada, established in 1992, is the market leader for UHT milk in Panama and also commercializes a range of dairy and non-dairy products. The company’s brands, “La Chiricana”, “Dos Pinos” and “Nevada,” hold a 60% market share at the local level. Strategically located in Panama’s main milk production area, Nevada operates as a 100% indirect subsidiary of Cooperativa de Productores de Leche Dos Pinos, Costa Rica.

Nevada’s business model involves purchasing milk from approximately 150 small farmers and producing high-quality milk and dairy products. National distribution is managed through Dicarina, a related distribution company with over 8,000 distribution points across Panama.

Renell Kokshetau LLP, Kazakhstan is a project company established with the purpose of design, build, finance, maintain of a state of the art 630 bed multispeciality hospital in Kokshetau, Northern Kazakhstan.

The project shareholders are Renell Co. Ltd and Rönesans Saglik Yatirim Anonim Sirketi ultimately owned by Rönesans Holding, Turkey

The business purpose of the project company is to improve and update Kazakhstan’s health infrastructure with a multi-purpose hospital facility for the Akmola region covering 10 cities, 17 districts, with a population of 733 thousand people and with Kazakhstan’s ministry of health as off-taker/user of the modern hospital.

JSC TBC Bank (TBC) was founded in 1992 as a universal bank and has since then become one of the largest banks in Georgia with a market share of approx. 40% in customer loans and deposits. TBC is a systemically important bank and is active in all business segments. The bank is the market leader in the retail segment and the leading partner bank for MSMEs offering them also extensive business support programs.

client_name: Vinte Viviendas Integrales, S.A.B. DE C.V.
description: Founded in 2001, Vinte Viviendas Integrales, S.A.B. de C.V. (Vinte) is a fully integrated homebuilder engaged in the design, development, construction, commercialization and delivery of affordable entry-level, middle-class and upper-income housing developments in Mexico. Vinte promotes EDGE certified housing by using sustainable building materials and efficient energy and water consumption. Based in Mexico City, the company has presence in six states across Mexico. By the acquisition of Servicios Corporativos Javer, S.A.B. de C.V. –  one of the biggest real estate developers in Mexico – Vinte will significantly increase its regional presence and enlarge its low-income housing portfolio.

Banco Promerica S.A. is a mid-sized universal bank in Guatemala. It was established in 1993 under the name of Banco Privado para el Desarrollo, S. A. (Bancasol). In 2007, Bancasol was acquired by Grupo Promerica and shortly thereafter renamed. The bank is part of the strong regional banking group Promerica with presence in seven Central American countries, namely Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Dominican Republic as well as Ecuador and the Cayman Islands. It is the region’s largest network of its kind which does not belong to an international bank.

Zona Franca Grecia, S.A. (ZFG) was founded in 2016 with the purpose of developing, operating, leasing and selling commercial premises of the industrial free-trade zone ‘Grecia’ with focus on healthcare / medical supplies in the western region of San José, Costa Rica.

Jungle Ventures is a well-established venture capital (VC) fund manager based in Singapore. Operating since 2012, the firm invests across India and Southeast Asia (SEA) and manages a total fund volume of over 1 billion USD  supporting more than 70 portfolio companies. Jungle Ventures V, L.P. is the fund manager’s fifth fund, with an anticipated total fund volume of USD 500 million.

Enerjisa Enerji Üretim A.S. (Enerjisa) is owned by renowned sponsors such as German utility company E.On and Turkish conglomerate Sabanci Group, and is one of the largest independent power producers in Turkey with an installed capacity of 3.8 GW and around 1,100 employees.

Starting its operations in 1998, CreditAccess Grameen Limited is one of the oldest and largest microfinance institutions in India. The company operates across the country through 2,031 branches in 16 states and one union territory as of September 2024. The main focus is providing micro loans to women predominantly in the rural areas of India.

Stanbic Bank Kenya Limited is part of the Standard Bank Group (SBG). Being a subsidiary of SBG, the bank offers a wide range of services to leading companies in Kenya and the region aligned to the Group’s purpose: “Africa is our home, we drive her growth”.

client_name: Banco Azul de El Salvador S.A.
description: Banco Azul de El Salvador S.A. (Banco Azul) is a bank that started its operations in El Salvador in 2015. Owned by local shareholders, it has developed a strong focus on servicing local small and medium-sized enterprises. It is a relatively small financial institution, with a market share of around 4% in terms of loans. Banco Azul is focused on supporting local entrepreneurs as well as promoting women leadership.

client_name: Cooperativa Central de Crédito com Interação Solidária Central Cresol Baser
description: Cooperativa Central de Crédito com Interação Solidária Central Cresol Baser is a professional and fast growing financial cooperative system in Brazil that was established in 1996. The cooperative focuses on providing loans and other financial and non-financial services to local individuals, micro, small and medium companies. It operates under the umbrella of the Cresol System, which is one of Brazil’s largest financial cooperative systems. The Cresol System is a member of the Amazon Finance Network, an international initiative launched by IFC and IDB Invest with the aim of generating sustainable impact across the Amazon region.

client_name: Cooperativa Central de Crédito com Interação Solidária Central Cresol Sicoper
description: Cooperativa Central de Crédito com Interação Solidária Central Cresol Sicoper is a professional and fast growing financial cooperative system in Brazil that was established in 2014. The cooperative focuses on providing loans and other financial and non-financial services to local individuals, micro, small and medium companies. It operates under the umbrella of the Cresol System, which is one of Brazil’s largest financial cooperative systems. The Cresol System is a member of the Amazon Finance Network, an international initiative launched by IFC and IDB Invest with the aim of generating sustainable impact across the Amazon region.

client_name: Amicus Capital Partners India Fund II
description: Amicus Capital Partners India Fund II is an India focused sector agnostic growth capital PE fund. It is managed by Amicus India Capital Partners LLP and headquartered in Bangalore. The current Fund II size stands at INR 15.7 billion. Amicus Capital currently has Assets under Management (AuM) of INR 22 billion (around USD 280 million) across two funds.

“Rönesans Holding A.S.” (RH) was established in 1993  in Turkey. RH operates as the main contractor and investor in construction, energy, healthcare, real estate and industrial investments in a wide geographical area with the main operating regions being Turkey, Central Asia and Europe. The business model of RH relies upon the free cash generated by construction activities, which are invested into strategic sectors that the holding has operations in.

Gulf Renewable Energy Company Limited (GRE) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited (GULF). Established in 2018 as GULF’s renewable energy investment arm, GRE has a total committed capacity of 6,059.5 MW, of which 1,935.2 MW is currently in operation (as of January 2025). The proposed transaction is backed by an unconditional and irrevocable first-demand guarantee from GULF.

Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited (GULF) was founded in 2007, and is a leading power gen-eration company in Thailand, holding the largest portfolio of contracted power purchase agreements (PPAs) in the country. As of January 2025, GULF has a total installed capacity of 15,870 MW.

Khan Bank is the largest commercial bank in Mongolia. With more than 500 branches nationwide it services over 80% of the Mongolian population. The bank provides a wide range of financial services including personal loans, business loans, mortgages, and savings products. DEG already invested in Khan Bank prior to this commitment. Info on the 2021 financing can be found here. [https://deginvest-investments.de/portfolio/khan-bank-llc-1]

XacBank JSC, founded in 2001, is a universal, private, and systemically important bank, ranking as the fourth largest commercial bank in Mongolia by assets. Headquartered in Ulaanbaatar, the bank serves approximately 1 million corporate, SME, and retail customers across Mongolia through a network of over 80 branches. As of the end of 2023, XacBank employs around 1,170 people, with women representing over 60% of its workforce.

Industrial Comercial San Martín is a Nicaraguan producer and distributor of beef meat and by-products. It was incorporated in Nandaime, Nicaragua in 1973 and is the largest player in this industry in Central America, as well as one of the largest exporters in Nicaragua. It holds livestock in its own feedlots, processes and sells meat together with other related products like bone meal, and produces biogas.

San Martin’s production model is focused on self-sustainability & eco-friendly production by generating its own renewable energy using its two digestors and biogas power plants and by substituting most of the fossil fuel usage in the production process.

client_name: AFRICON (Connect GmbH & Co. geschlossene Invest KG)
description: AFRICON is an investment vehicle set up and funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). It is used to fund investments of the program ImpactConnect. AFRICON is man-aged by fund manager CREDION. AFRICON supports companies with a proven link to the European Union (EU) with loans up to EUR 5 million that have a high developmental impact in developing countries, especially by creating or maintaining local employment. With the global expansion of the fund’s strategy in 2024, there are 84 target countries in Africa, Latin America, Non-EU-Eastern Europe countries and Middle East.

Milšped d.o.o. (Milšped), founded in 1993 in Serbia, is a leading Serbian logistic solutions provider covering complete cycle of freight logistics from forwarding and custom clearance, sea and air transport brokerage, international road transport, warehousing services to last-mile courier services. With 20 subsidiaries located in the EU, South-East Europe, USA and Asia, Milšped is a key logistics partner of local corporates and multinationals mostly in FMCG, pharmaceutical and automotive sectors.

Creador is an independent fund manager operating since 2011 with in total USD 2.2 bn raised over five funds and investments into 57 companies across India and South East Asia (“SEA”). With Creador VI DEG is now supporting the fund manager’s 6th fund with an anticipated fund volume of 900 m USD.

The fund will predominantly target significant minority stakes in high growth businesses operating within retail, consumer products & services, healthcare, financial services, business services and technology sub-sectors across SEA and India.

Creador is headquartered in Malaysia, with total headcount of 56 personnel in the investment team.

BDO Network Bank is the largest rural bank in the Philippines, operating through 333 branches and 120 credit offices, primarily serving underserved rural regions in Davao and northern Luzon. Founded in 1952 in Davao, the bank expanded by merging with other rural banks in the 1990s and early 2000s. In July 2015, it became a wholly owned subsidiary of BDO Unibank and was rebranded as BDO Network Bank in August 2019.

The Anglesey Food Limited (“Korzinka” or “company”) was founded in 1996 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, and is the largest food retailer in the country. The company is a pioneer of formal retail, operates ca. 140 stores and holds a leading, 50% market share in the organized food retail market.

Banco de América Central, S.A. is the fourth largest bank in Guatemala, operating a full service universal bank model. The customer segments enterprises and retail clients are approximately equal in size.
Wi-Net Telecom S.A.C. is the third largest fixed broad-band supplier in Peru and the leading optical fiber-to-the-home provider for private households in the country.

Tradewind was established in 2000 in Germany with a first focus in/on Turkey as an international factoring company providing tailor-made working capital solutions to exporters in DEG’s markets. Importers are located in Europe and North America for the main part. Tradewind has offices in Istanbul, Karachi, Dhaka, Shanghai, New York, Sofia, Budapest, and Dubai.

Terabank is a mid-sized bank in Georgia, providing financial services to retail, SME and corporate clients. The bank was established in 2007, and operates since 2016 under the name Terabank.

Terabank specializes in financing small and medium-sized enterprises. It operates through a network of 32 branches across Georgia.

Torrecom Partners LP (“Torrecom”) was established in 2010. Torrecom and its subsidiaries are one of the largest build-to-suit (BTS) telecommunication tower companies in Latin America. The company operates in Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, Mexico, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Chile, and Paraguay. Torrecom owns and operates a network of approximately 1,400+ sites for mobile communication across these countries, enabling mobile telecommunication carriers to focus on providing services to their subscribers.

Aspen group is the biggest South African pharma group focused on manufacturing and commercialization of generics, including sterile injectables and active pharmaceutical ingredients, at a global level. The borrower Aspen Treasury Ireland Limited is a subsidiary of Aspen Pharmacare Holdings Limited, which is listed at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

Before this commitment, DEG had already invested in Aspen in 2021. [https://deginvest-investments.de/portfolio/aspen-finance-proprietary-limited]

Arpe Ltd is a project company established to develop, construct, and operate two run-of-river hydropower plants with capacities of 42 MW and 41 MW, respectively, in northern Uganda.
