Ce projet, porté par la Fondation Grameen Crédit Agricole avec l’appui de PROPARCO, vise à élargir l’accès à des services financiers adaptés pour les réfugiés, les populations déplacées et les communautés hôtes. Il apporte un soutien direct à deux institutions de microfinance en Ouganda : VisionFund et UGAFODE.

Le programme prévoit notamment des formations pour les institutions de microfinance et leurs clients, le développement de produits financiers inclusifs – en particulier à destination des femmes –, ainsi qu’un accompagnement à la digitalisation et des actions de capitalisation et de communication.

Il s'agit d'une assistance technique (AT) financée par l'Union européenne pour soutenir la gestion du programme MSME Platform. Cette AT est mise en oeuvre par EDFI MC. L'AT couvre principalement les coûts de gestion du programme ainsi que les activités de coordination, de suivi de portefeuille et de communication

Le fonds RNAF III est un fonds de capital-investissement dédié à l’Afrique du Nord, à l’exception de la Libye, avec un intérêt marqué pour le marché égyptien. Sa stratégie d’investissement vise à accompagner la croissance d’entreprises opérant dans des secteurs portés par les dynamiques structurelles de la région, notamment l’essor démographique, l’urbanisation, l’augmentation des revenus et la digitalisation de l’économie. Le fonds cible principalement des sociétés de taille intermédiaire actives dans les secteurs de la consommation, de la santé, de l’éducation et des services financiers, à travers des investissements majoritaires ou minoritaires.

S’appuyant sur une équipe disposant d’une solide expérience d’investissement dans la région — notamment en Égypte et dans le secteur de la santé — le fonds bénéficie d’une présence locale à travers des bureaux régionaux et d’un réseau établi. RNAF III adopte une approche généraliste orientée vers des entreprises rentables présentant un fort potentiel de croissance, avec l’ambition d’accompagner l’émergence de leaders nationaux, régionaux voire continentaux.

Proparco souscrit en tant qu'investisseur d'ancrage à hauteur de 7,5 milliards de XOF (11,4 millions d'euros) à une émission obligataire de la CRRH-UEMOA cotée sur la Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières de l'UEMOA (Abidjan), labellisée obligations sociales pour la première fois et ambitionnant de lever jusqu'à 60 milliards de XOF. Cette intervention soutient le financement du logement abordable dans la zone UEMOA, en faveur des ménages à revenus modestes souhaitant accéder à la propriété de leur résidence principale.

The Company has established a strong reputation in electric vehicles. It is, with the support of USD 135 million syndicated debt arranged by ADB, expanding its electric bus manufacturing operations and charging network.

Societe JTF Madagascar SARL was established by the Italian renewable energy company Tozzi Green SpA in 2010. The company now concentrates on food crops such as maize, soya beans and geranium cultivation. The company produces food and feed crops for the local market. The Project Company operates a large-scale farm in Satrokala and Andiolava towns in the district of Ihosy, about 660 km from Antananarivo. The farm is entirely supported by independent wind and solar energy and is not connected to the grid. Societe JTF Madagascar aims to expand cultivation from 5,425 hectares to 6,981 hectares.

XacBank is Finnfund's former client, and the previous facility was prepaid in 2023. The loan strengthens XacBank’s on-lending capacity in its MSME activities and directs a large part of the loan proceeds to female entrepreneurs in Mongolia.

San Francisco S.A. is a Paraguayan company which owns and operates two harbours by the Paraguay River. The company is building a new modern harbour in Villeta, which is located about 40 km south from Asunción, the capital. Finnfund invests in the new harbour in Villeta and participates in re-financing the company's existing debt portfolio and other development financing institutions. The new Villetan harbour will give Paraguayan products better access to international markets.

The company's activities include loading and unloading the cargo of ships and barges, storing and maintaining containers, and other stevedoring and logistic services. About 90% of the company's business is related to container handling. The company is using technology supplied by Finnish companies Cargotec and Kalmar.

The fund is managed by Arbaro Advisors GmbH, which employs the fund's management team. The Arbaro Advisors GmbH is owned by forest consulting and management company Unique and asset advisory company Finance in motion.

Sanergy aims to build healthy, prosperous communities by making hygienic sanitation affordable and accessible throughout Nairobi’s informal settlements. Sanergy converts waste into valuable end-products such as fertilisers, animal feed, and biogas. With funding provided by Finnfund, the company is expanding its activities in Nairobi and other parts of Kenya.
Sanergy co-composts waste with sawdust, other carbon sources, and effective micro-organisms to produce fertiliser, eliminating pathogens. Then, the compost is left to mature in windrows. Once ready, every batch of fertiliser is tested by third parties to ensure compliance with World Health Organization standards. Sanergy has a colony of Black Solider Flies, whose larvae consume organic waste, removing the pathogens and converting the waste into protein to produce insect-based animal feed. Boiled and sun-dried to eliminate pathogens, the larvae make a sustainably produced, nutrient-rich protein input for animal feed. 100% of the waste is safely treated.
The company produces pellets in Surabaya, Indonesia, using residues from the mechanical forest industry, mainly the furniture manufacturing industry. Pellets are burnt to generate renewable energy.

Sathapana Bank is the 5th largest bank in Cambodia, focusing on MSME and SME clients in rural areas, specifically in commerce and agriculture. In September 2020, it had approximately USD 1.7 billion in customer loans, total assets were USD 2 billion, and over 4,000 employees and 171 branches.
Sathapana is pursuing a growth strategy to broaden its client base and to become a top-three player in the market, and it is seeking Tier 2 capital to enable this growth. Sathapana is an existing client of Finnfund. Finnfund provided a senior loan of USD 11 million to Sathapana Microfinance in 2015 and a Tier 2 loan of USD 10 million in 2019. The senior loan was part of the FMO syndicate and has been fully repaid.
Sathapana Bank is a bank in Cambodia that finances retail, micro companies, and SME clients. At the end of 2018, it had approximately 131,000 loan customers, over 4,000 employees and 160 branches.

SATYA MicroCapital Ltd is one of the fastest-growing non-banking finance companies for microfinance (NBFC-MFI), providing microcredit across the country in rural parts of India. The company started its operations in January 2017. Within five years, it has rapidly expanded operations in 22 states (out of 36 states and union territories in India) with a loan portfolio of USD 321 million and 1.1 million customers. 
The company exclusively caters the unserved and underserved women population in low-income households for entrepreneurship and income generation purposes. Through small credit provision, SATYA aims to empower women in rural areas and improve their socio-economic livelihood.

Proximity Finance Microfinance Company Limited is Myanmar’s first farmer-focused finance institution. Proximity Finance was launched in 2010 as the microfinance arm of Proximity Designs. Proximity Designs is one of Myanmar's largest agricultural services platforms, providing farm technology, advice, and financial services to small family farms across the country. Proximity Finance serves over 130,000 smallholder farmer households through 16 branches, reaching 2,000 villages in 9 of Myanmar’s 14 states and regions.
Finnfund participates with USD 4.7 million equity in Proximity Finance’s USD 14 million equity package together with Nordic Microfinance Initiative (NMI) and Proparco. The funds will be used to increase loan sizes to adequately meet the capital requirements of small farms to boost farm yields and profits, diversify Proximity Finance’s financial product offering, and invest in technology and systems to grow the gross loan portfolio and double the active smallholder farmer client base.

PT Amartha Mikro Fintek (“Amartha”) is Indonesia’s leading microfinance fintech, focusing on providing loans and other financial inclusion products to low-income households with limited or no access to financial services. It actively provides services in rural areas of the Indonesian archipelago, serving around 1.2 million rural female microentrepreneurs. By leveraging its Peer-to-Peer (P2P) fintech license Amartha connects retail and institutional investors with underserved borrowers. Finnfund’s senior loan will go to Inclusive Capital Fund Pte. Ltd., an SPV that will channel funding to Amartha’s customers.

Menengai is a 35 MW greenfield geothermal project and part of the first phase of the wider Menengai complex, which is the second large-scale geothermal field being developed in Kenya after Olkaria. Globeleq will operate and maintain the power plant once it has reached commercial operations in 2025.
Steam will be supplied to the project by Geothermal Development Company (GDC), a Kenya government-owned company under a 25-year project implementation and steam supply agreement (PISSA). Once operational, electricity will be sold to Kenya Power, the national distribution company, under a power purchase agreement (PPA) for the same timeframe. The project also benefits from a signed and effective Letter of Support from the Government of Kenya. The project will deliver clean and cheap baseload power to the national grid, enabling GDC to monetise the available steam resources from the Menengai steam field.

Finnfund is joining an FMO syndicated loan facility of USD 50 million. The facility will be used for the construction of processing facilities in Ivory Coast (cashew nuts), Burkina Faso (sesame seeds), and Mozambique (sesame seeds) and for working capital.

Siddhartha Bank is currently among the 10 largest banks in Nepal, with a network of almost 200 branches spread across the country, including many remote areas. Finnfund’s loan proceeds will be used to facilitate loan portfolio growth, specifically Siddhartha’s MSME, agribusiness, and hydropower loan portfolios.

A Finnish solar power group, Solar Finland, and a Thai public utility, PEA Encom, established a modern, automated solar panel factory in Thailand. The capacity of the factory is 100 MWp a year. The 7.5 million euro investment will be financed by equity, of which Finnfund provides approximately 37%, Solar Finland about 38 % and PEA Encom 25%. The primary market of the factory is Thailand, but it will target the neighbouring markets too.

San Francisco S.A. is a Paraguayan company which owns and operates two harbours by the Paraguay River. The company is building a new modern harbour in Villeta, which is located about 40 km south from Asunción, the capital. Finnfund invests in the new harbour in Villeta and participates in re-financing the company's existing debt portfolio and other development financing institutions. The new Villetan harbour will give Paraguayan products better access to international markets.

The company's activities include loading and unloading the cargo of ships and barges, storing and maintaining containers, and other stevedoring and logistic services. About 90% of the company's business is related to container handling. The company is using technology supplied by Finnish companies Cargotec and Kalmar.

A holding company has been established together with the Norway-based Norsk Solar SA to fund and own power solutions with solar photovoltaic (PV) components for commercial and industrial (C&I) and utility clients with a targeted aggregated capacity of 50 MW in Finnfund’s target markets.
The geographical scope is global. A significant portion of projects is expected to be in C&I projects in Vietnam.

client_name: OP Finnfund Global Impact Fund I
description: As Finland's first global impact investment fund, the OP Finnfund Global Impact Fund I provides professional investors a means to promote the UN SDGs' achievement by investing in high-impact projects in developing markets.

Penda Health is a chain of affordable medical centres in Nairobi, Kenya.
They operate a network of medical centres that offer outpatient primary healthcare services up to 83% cheaper than those offered by other high-quality private healthcare providers. The company provides comprehensive outpatient health services, including obstetrics, gynaecology, dental services, lab testing, maternal health services and preventative care, among other primary healthcare services.
Penda plans to open a network of over 100 medical centres across East Africa, ensuring that medical services are available to most of the underserved low-income consumers in the region.

Phatisa Food Fund 2 is a pan-African fund focusing on African agriculture and the food value chain, focusing on inputs to food production, integrated food production and processing, food manufacturing, and fast-moving consumer goods and food service.

Polykrome is one of Senegal’s largest industrial printing companies, which has begun to refocus its business from printing and graphics to packaging solutions such as cardboard and plastic film labels, which local consumer goods manufacturers mainly use.
Finnfund’s loan is part of a financing package syndicated by IFC, a member of the World Bank Group. It will be used to expand the company’s production and relocate its existing facilities to a new industrial site. The aim is to support local production of packaging solutions and foster local production and distribution of consumer goods.

Miro Forestry Developments Limited is a forestry company with two subsidiaries in Ghana and Sierra Leone. Miro is a vertically integrated, sustainable forestry and timber products business focused on fast-growing, high-yield plantation timber to produce sawn timber, utility poles and plywood for local and international markets.
Miro has demonstrated competence in land preparation, planting, forestry management and species selection, successfully planting ca. 20,000 hectares.
Finnfund has invested in Miro since 2014. The new funding is deployed to increase Miro’s downstream processing capacity, particularly plywood.

client_name: Pro Eucalipto Holding S.A.P.I. de C.V.

description: Finnfund is providing a USD 10 million loan to finance the expansion project of MLR Forestal de Nicaragua, a forestry company operating teak and cocoa plantations. The company will sell most of its certified teak through international traders in Indian and other Asian markets. The fine cocoa produced is sold in the local Nicaraguan market, but global markets will be sourced as production continues to increase. MLR plans to expand its planted area by another 1,900 hectares to reach approximately 4,500 hectares.

client_name: Pro Eucalipto Holding S.A.P.I. de C.V.

description:
Finnfund provides financing for Procarsa, one of the leading packaging companies in Ecuador, and paper mill Surpapelcorp.
Surpapelcorp uses recycled corrugated and cardboard materials in its paper production process. The company has created its recycled waste paper supply chain (a subsidiary called RePapers). Procarsa mainly uses paper produced by Surpapelcorp in its cardboard box production.
Finnfund is providing sustainable long-term financing and working capital for the borrowers.

Mountain Hazelnuts is a regenerative agriculture company operating in Bhutan. The company works with ca. 8,000 smallholders and has planted more than 1,700 ha of hazelnut plantations since 2011. The business model is based on a partnership with the smallholders and the government of Bhutan. Mountain Hazelnuts produces the seedlings at an existing nursery while planting as well as maintenance of the trees and harvesting of the crop is done by the farmers. Mountain Hazelnuts provides technical, logistical, and operational support and pre-agreed offtake for the hazelnuts. Hazelnuts are sold by Mountain Hazelnuts in-shell or kernel to export markets – mainly to Western premium markets.

The funding is used to further scale the operations from the current 1,700 ha to 4,800 ha of hazelnut orchards. In addition, Mountain Hazelnuts will invest additional capex to scale and upgrade the processing facility to match the increasing hazelnut harvest volumes.

Nafoods Group Joint Stock Company is a Vietnamese fruit manufacturer and exporter with a leading position in passion fruits. The Company is engaged in the production and sales of fruit concentrate and puree, frozen fruit products, passion fruit seedlings, dried fruits and fresh fruits, covering the entire fruit processing value chain from planting to sales. Nafoods group utilizes over 30 different fruits and vegetables in processing varying with seasonality of harvest, including passion fruit, banana, kumquat, pineapple, mango, ginger, coconut, dragon fruit, pomelo, lime, and lychee etc. Finnfund’s financing will be used for the contruction of dried fruit manufacturing plant.

IDB Invest and Finnfund have invested USD 5 million of equity with Netwey, a Mexican Internet Service Provider, to facilitate accessible internet through an expanded fibre optic network. This investment is designed to enable a larger number of low-income households to gain access to unlimited high-speed internet.

The project aims to broaden Netwey's fibre optic network, thus enabling more low-income households to access high-speed internet. Broadband services have a transformative impact on the economy and society, providing numerous benefits ranging from more productive businesses and efficient public services to empowering individuals with knowledge and information.

New Forests Company is a forest plantation and processing company with three operating companies in Tanzania, Uganda, and Rwanda. The Group Companies have planted over 20,000 hectares of trees and are estimated to sequester over 200,000 tCO2e annually. The New Forests Company has pole plants in each country and sawmills in Uganda and Rwanda.

New Forests Company is a forest plantation and processing company with three operating companies in Tanzania, Uganda, and Rwanda. The Group Companies have planted over 20,000 hectares of trees and are estimated to sequester over 200,000 tCO2e annually. The New Forests Company has pole plants in each country and sawmills in Uganda and Rwanda.
The investment will support the transition to cleaner and cheaper travel alternatives by accelerating the availability and adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in India.

Kasha is an e-commerce platform improving women’s access to genuine health, hygiene and self-care products in East Africa. The company sells menstrual care products, contraceptives, pharmaceuticals and a range of beauty products via its platform, accessible through basic phones and a website and delivered to customers confidentially. Kasha aims to be a trusted source of information, especially around stigmatised products and operates in close cooperation with selected health partners.

Kasha was founded in 2015 in Rwanda and has since expanded to Kenya. The company has served over 600,000 customers, of whom 61% are women. With Finnfund’s investment, Kasha looks to grow its presence in current markets and expand to South and West Africa.

Metier Capital Growth Fund III is a generalist private equity fund focusing on deploying growth capital into entrepreneurial businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa. The Metier Group manages the fund. The fund targets a total size of USD 200 million, and a strong first close was achieved at USD 182 million in September 2023.

Kashf Foundation is an existing client of Finnfund, and the previous facility matured in early 2024. With the new loan, Kashf will continue on-lending business loans to its customers. 
Kashf is registered as a Non-Banking Micro Finance Company, and it is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Its customers are low-income households, especially women. 
Financial services include appraisal-backed individual lending along with other non-financial services that have a transformative impact at the household level. Non-financial services include capacity building by offering skills development training to better understand the products and services.

Inspiring Development sought to establish a new microfinance company called Oasis Credit (Mikrokredit Tashkiloti Oasiscredit (Oasis)) in Uzbekistan, one of the few remaining underdeveloped microfinance markets in Asia.

Kentegra Biotechnology produces Pale Refined Extract from the pyrethrum flower sourced from smallholders in Kenya. The extract is a 100% natural ingredient in manufacturing insecticides, pesticides, and other agricultural and household formulations.

Finnfund is investing USD 5 million in equity to support building a new processing facility in Kenya to expand the production capacity.

Kentegra Biotechnology produces Pale Refined Extract from the pyrethrum flower sourced from smallholders in Kenya. The extract is used as a 100% natural ingredient in the manufacturing of insecticides, pesticides, and other agricultural and household formulations.

Finnfund has invested USD 0.5 million to support operations in Kenya.

Miro Forestry Developments Limited is a forestry company with two subsidiaries in Ghana and Sierra Leone. Miro is a vertically integrated, sustainable forestry and timber products business focused on fast-growing, high-yield plantation timber to produce sawn timber, utility poles and plywood for both local and international markets. Miro has demonstrated competence in land preparation, planting, forestry management and species selection, successfully planting over 15,000 hectares. Finnfund has invested in Miro since 2014. The new funding is deployed to expand Miro’s plantation area and to increase downstream processing capacity

Finnfund has made a USD 15 million investment into Khan Bank in Mongolia as part of a USD 200 million multi-currency FMO led syndication facility, alongside FMO and CDP, Italian’s DFI and a group of private and impact investors. Khan Bank is the leading and largest universal bank in Mongolia, playing a pivotal role in the country’s banking sector and is known for its strong customer-centric approach, leadership in sustainable finance and leading market position. It serves more than 82% of Mongolian’s population through an extensive network of over 47 branches and diverse digital channels. Its comprehensive banking services reach individuals, SMEs and corporate customers across both urban and remote regions in Mongolia, driven by a strategic focus on digitalization, rural enterprise support and sustainability.  

The Bank holds a B3 rating from Moody's and a B+ rating from Fitch, both with a stable outlook. Khan Bank has made significant strides in sustainable finance, including the launch of Mongolia's first green bond in 2023, followed by the issuance of the country's first social bond in 2024. The investment is 2X Challenge-aligned, where FMO and Finnfund will allocate over 30% of their loan and CDP contributing 30% of half of their loan, to women-owned or women-led enterprises, meeting the 2X Challenge criteria. The loan proceeds are targeted towards green financing 30% and the remainder 70% towards Women/Youth/Agri SMEs and certified SMEs in the sustainable cashmere industry. The loan will support the Bank’s strategy and its mission to build a greener, more inclusive Mongolia.

Kilombero Valley Teak Company (KVTC) was established in 1992 and is one of Africa's most innovative forest management projects, bringing a wide range of social, economic and environmental benefits to a remote area of Tanzania.
At the heart of the project are the planting and sustainable harvesting of plantation teak and the protection and management of over 20,000 ha of native forests and wetlands and a wide range of wildlife and flora within.
KVTC has established an integrated processing plant to produce timber and value-added products, bringing long-term employment and social development to the region.

Lona Group is a vertically integrated fruit food business in South Africa. Established in 1996 and headquartered in Cape Town, Lona Group markets and exports citrus fruit from its farms and on behalf of other producers. The company has expanded into agro-processing, logistics, and services during the past decade. Finnfund co-invests in Lona Holdco, which owns the majority of Lona Group, together with Phatisa Food Fund 2, BII, and Norfund.
The expansion investments with the equity capital relate mainly to the expansion of food and fruit product processing capacity, cold storage-related investments, orchard net investments, small orchard expansion on selected farms, and finally to corporate acquisitions, which relate to buying out minority shareholders of group chosen entities.

Yumn Ltd will construct, own and operate an 80 MW peat-fired power plant in Rwanda. The company also has a long-term concession for harvesting the fuel. The power will be supplied to the national grid. The project will have a Finnish boiler, other power-related technology, and peat harvesting technology. The project will also benefit from Finnish operations and maintenance experience, having Fortum as the O&M contractor.

KaiOS Technologies is the leading mobile Operating System (OS) for smart feature phones and the third largest OS after Android and iOS. The company has shipped over 170 million devices and has over 190 models available, including Nokia phones. With Finnfund’s investment, KaiOS can expand into new markets in Sub-Saharan Africa.
The investment is classified as a 2X Challenge eligible gender investment as it supports women to close the digital divide across lower-middle-income countries. KaiOS brings a more affordable device to the market and hosts applications and content targeting women and girls.

description:
Kasha is an e-commerce platform improving women’s access to health, hygiene, and self-care products in East Africa. The company sells a range of menstrual care products, contraceptives, pharmaceuticals, and beauty products via its platform. Kasha aims to act as a trusted source of information about women’s products and operates in close cooperation with selected health partners.
Kasha’s products and services are accessible through the web platform, with a basic phone, and via an agent network to serve women in rural areas. Last-mile delivery to customers is handled confidentially.
Kasha was founded in 2016 in Rwanda and has since expanded to Kenya. The company has delivered over 830,000 products to over 100,000 consumers, over 80,000 of whom are direct customers and 75% of whom are low-income. With Finnfund’s investment, Kasha looks to grow its presence in current markets and expand and pilot its concept in three new African countries.

Founded in 2013, Hewa Tele is an affordable medical oxygen provider, operating three Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) plants in Kenya and offering a full range of services across the medical oxygen value chain. With Finnfund’s financing, Hewa Tele is expanding its capacity and constructing a liquid oxygen manufacturing facility to address the oxygen supply gap in East Africa.

Horizon Capital Growth Fund IV (HCGF IV) is a USD 300 million target private equity fund that will provide growth equity capital to high-quality, fast-growing SME and mid-cap technology (IT) and export-oriented companies in Ukraine and Moldova. Finnfund’s investment will support these companies’ continued growth, as these companies are in much need of capital, which is in very short supply due to the war in Ukraine. The companies’ growth will, in turn, lead to job creation, including jobs for women.

HCGF IV is the first fund in Eastern Europe which has been qualified as a 2X Challenge Flagship Fund. The Fund will strive to invest in female entrepreneurs and support gender parity in its portfolio companies, noting that women are underrepresented in the technology/IT sector, in general, and in Ukraine. 

HCGF IV will be managed by the Ukrainian-based Horizon Capital. The Horizon team have been investing in Ukraine and Moldova since the mid-1990s, and Horizon Capital currently has more than USD 1,2 billion in Assets under Management. HCGF IV is the Manager’s 6th fund.

The project company was founded to construct and operate a 50 MW solar power plant in Benban, South Egypt. The solar PV power plant is one of about 30 plants to be built on the same 3,700-hectare site in Benban. The Benban site’s total power production will be around 1.5 GW. Electricity produced in the plant will be sold to the government-owned Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company with a long-term power purchase agreement, benefitting the people of Egypt with low-cost renewable electricity.

Hospital Holdings Investment is an established special-purpose vehicle to finance the acquisition and integration of targeted healthcare services businesses in East and Southern Africa.
They have invested in the following projects: AAR Hospital (Kenya), AAR Healthcare (Uganda), Kampala Hospital (Uganda), and Nakasero Hospital (Uganda).

Humania is an established special-purpose vehicle to finance the development of high-quality multispecialty hospitals and healthcare assets in North Africa and Pakistan. Bait Al Batterjee Medical Co will establish Humania and initially focus on four projects in Egypt and Morocco. All assets will be operated under the Saudi German Hospital banner.

Igloo is an InsurTech, established in 2016 as Axinan Pte Ltd, with a mission to provide “Insurance for All” by making insurance accessible through technology. Igloo provides non-life microinsurance products to customers across Southeast Asia, with Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines as the key target markets.
Tech platform allows tapping into an underserved market that is difficult for traditional insurance companies to address. Igloo has processed over 250 million policies, with an average policy size of 20 US cents.
Low insurance penetration and high mobile penetration in the region allow the potential for GWP growth.

ICCF finances renewable energy and energy efficiency projects in the private sector in developing countries and emerging markets. ICCF was established to facilitate an efficient and fast-track process with low administrative overheads for co-financing between European DFIs, EIB, and AFD.
Finnfund participates already in the fourth round of financing via ICCF. The track record of co-financing via this instrument is positive.

description:
IPT Powertech Group (IPT), established in 2006, specialises in providing energy solutions for mobile network operators (MNOs) in emerging markets. Its special focus area is the energy supply of telecom towers with hybrid solutions, i.e., a combination of solar panels, batteries, and diesel generators. 

The main purpose of the loan is to support the growth of IPT group operations and projects in chosen countries. This loan is part of the DEG-led syndicate of USD 80 million. Finnfund share of the financing is USD 15.4 million, bringing its total exposure to approximately USD 18 million. IPT has a strong role in transforming the telecom industry energy base from climate-negative and fossil fuel-based sources to energy-efficient and renewable sources, which fits well into Finnfund’s broader climate strategy.

The project involves modernising the energy supply infrastructure in (T-ESCO-contracts) Lebanon and Guinea. With financing from Finnfund, DEG, Proparco and the European Investment Bank, IPT will modernise the energy supply infrastructure in Lebanon and Guinea. The hybrid solution utilising solar panels and storage media will save up to 40% of energy and reduce diesel consumption significantly.

JUMO World Limited is the largest-scale, lowest-cost financial services platform for Emerging Markets. JUMO is a transaction and predictive technology platform for mobile network operators and banks operating in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
JUMO offers a diversified product base that drives customer utility, including mass-market credit and savings products. JUMO’s primary products, mobile loans, lending to airtime credit agents and business cash advances (BCA), use proprietary technology and partnerships with mobile network operators to tap markets that enjoy high mobile money usage but suffer from low penetration of traditional banking. Credit extended to new customers is initially relatively small and short-term, with limits increasing as their track record and behavioural dataset develop.

JUMO drives financial inclusion and creates value for mobile network operators and financial services providers. JUMO is also building a content-rich database on its millions of customers; JUMO expects this figure to grow significantly, allowing it to build a pan-African credit bureau.

JUMO boasts an experienced board and management team that includes founders of successful fintech businesses and other businesses in Africa.

description:
Fibertime Group is the parent company of Fibertime and Vulacoin. Fibertime provides a pay-as-you-go model of affordable and uncapped time-based open-access aerial fibre internet. Vulacoin provides a gateway for internet services providers to initiate micro digital payments at low costs for users to purchase internet and offer additional services through digital means.

With Finnfund ‘s investment, Fibertime Group will expand their operations into new townships in South Africa and software development.

First City Monument Bank Ltd is among Nigeria’s ten biggest commercial banks. It finances retail, micro, SME and corporate clients. The bank’s strategic goal is to grow its SME and retail portfolio, facilitating financial inclusion among underserved clientele and in agribusiness.
The Bank has in-house and client-focused incentives and programmes to support and encourage women’s participation in employment and entrepreneurship. The loan will support the growth of the bank’s lending to local and women-empowered businesses involved in the transformative sectors of agribusiness, manufacturing, health, and renewable energy. At a minimum, 30% of the loan proceeds will be channelled to women-owned businesses.

Finnfund’s financing is part of a DEG-led loan syndicate of USD 85 million, including Proparco and Norfund as co-lenders. Finnfund’s proposed financing is allocated to a newly formed bank through the merger of GHL Bank Limited and First National Bank Ghana following the acquisition of GHL Bank by FNB Ghana. Participation in this transaction will support the development of the nascent Ghanaian mortgage market and provide increased possibilities for lower-income household home ownership.

Forest First Colombia is establishing a large-scale forest plantation in Vichada Province, Colombia.
The Company will plant its land area with fast-growing hardwood tree species for various uses such as pulp, bioenergy and fibreboard. The Company uses modern technology and sustainable forest management practices and has an experienced international forestry management team. All native forest areas are set aside for conservation purposes.

description:
Fuzu Limited is a Kenyan-Finnish company that launched the Fuzu employment platform in 2015.
Fuzu is an online career and recruitment platform that provides job seekers with access to career advice, online learning and jobs. For employers, it provides a set of tools for identifying the best matching candidates via search and recruitment solutions and automated analysis of CVs. The platform integrates online psychometric testing and talent profiling of candidates into the application process.
Fuzu aims to combine the strengths of the Finnish education and innovation systems with a deep understanding of the end-users, their needs and aspirations in the African context. In Kenya, as in many other countries, the unemployment rate is very high, and young people are having difficulties entering the workforce. Fuzu aims to help people embark on meaningful careers and build better lives and help companies find the right talent.
Finnfund participates in financing Fuzu’s expansion in Kenya and the launch of the platform in selected geographies in Africa and Asia.

Fuzu is a career development, learning and recruitment platform developer and operator in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria. The company aims to provide a reliable and intelligent recruitment platform that brings the African job market online.
Fuzu is currently the number one career platform in East Africa and among the top 40 websites in Kenya, measured by visitor traffic. The company has about 350,000 unique monthly visitors and over 5,000 daily applications.
Finnfund invested with Sparkmind to finance the B2B operations growth in the current key markets in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

European Financing Partners (EFP), a joint venture between the European Investment Bank (EIB) and twelve European Development Finance Institutions (EDFIs), is a co-financing vehicle established in 2003 aiming at promoting sustainable development of the private sector and strengthening cooperation between eligible EDFIs and the EIB.

EIB’s financing is from the Cotonou Agreement Investment Facility for the African, Caribbean and Pacific Group of Countries (ACP) based on the Cotonou Agreement of July 2000. This means that EIB will only participate in projects in the ACP countries, whereas other shareholders of EFP can provide financing to countries included in the OECD DAC list.

description:
European Financing Partners (EFP), a joint venture between the European Investment Bank (EIB) and twelve European Development Finance Institutions (EDFIs), is a co-financing vehicle established in 2003 aiming at promoting sustainable development of the private sector and strengthening cooperation between eligible EDFIs and the EIB.

EIB’s financing is from the Cotonou Agreement Investment Facility for the African, Caribbean and Pacific Group of Countries (ACP) based on the Cotonou Agreement of July 2000. This means that EIB will only participate in projects in the ACP countries, whereas other shareholders of EFP can provide financing to countries included in the OECD DAC list.
EFP shareholders have committed nearly EUR 1.3 billion of financing over the years. This is the seventh round of commitments from the EDFI members to EFP, aimed at alleviating the consequences of the novel coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic for developing economies. Finnfund reactivates its participation in EFP with a EUR 10 million commitment dedicated solely to combat the consequences of the COVID-19 crisis.

Gemco Kati Exploration Pvt. Ltd. is a mineral exploration company owned by Finnish Oy Kati Ab and Indian founders. The company was founded in 2010 in Chandrapur, India, and it conducts drilling services mainly for mining prospectors and Indian authorities. Finnfund’s financing is targeted to enable the company’s further expansion by adding high-quality rigs and support vehicles into its fleet.

Evolution II is a 10-year closed-ended fund with a mandate for equity and equity-related investments into two principal investment streams: development and project finance infrastructure-type investments in clean and sustainable energy and growth equity investments in energy and resource efficiency companies and the value chains that support them.

Finnfund committed USD 20 million to the first close of Evolution III Fund. It is a Pan-Africa fund focusing on investments in renewable and sustainable energy infrastructure, energy access, and energy efficiency solutions. The fund is advised by a South Africa-based fund manager Inspired Evolution.

Finnfund has invested in Communication & Renewable Energy Infrastructure (CREI) to provide energy as a service to a telecom stakeholder in South Sudan by developing, building, operating, and maintaining energy assets.

Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund is a private equity fund that will seek to make up to 12 investments across Sub-Saharan Africa. The fund is the third investment vehicle of Convergence Partners (CP). CP's strategy is to invest in the digital infrastructure sector primarily by way of growth capital. Digital Infrastructure is critical for the African continent to leapfrog into the digital services world. People will benefit from improved digital infrastructure services directly and indirectly, and the services will provide improved business opportunities, services and employment opportunities. There is a major gap in financing digital infrastructures vs. the needs, and thus, the fund will allow and speed up this development.

Co-operative Bank of Kenya Ltd was founded in 1965 as a bank for the cooperative movement in Kenya. While having a strong cooperative identity and being the principal banker for the cooperative movement in Kenya, the Bank has evolved into a universal, third-largest bank in Kenya. A significant portion of Co-op Bank´s clientele is individuals and MSMEs. The loan proceeds will be used to support the MSME loan portfolio growth, which will facilitate financial inclusion among underserved clientele.

description:
Darby International Capital Latin American Fund IV is a closed-end private credit fund focusing on Latin America. The fund will target various sectors including infrastructure and logistics, natural resources and agribusiness industries, manufacturing, healthcare and consumer products.

The target commitment amount of the fund is USD 400 million.

The fund will target investing at least 50% of the total commitments in projects related to climate change mitigation and/or adaptation.

Geographically, the fund will focus on Latin America (primary countries being Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru).

The fund will be managed by Darby International Capital LLC.

description: Dolma provides capital and expertise to growth companies in Nepal. The fund is designed to generate sustainable private-sector employment and stimulate further Foreign Direct Investment into Nepal.

Cassava is a market-leading and diversified information and communications technology (ICT) platform in Africa. Operating in over 30 countries, Cassava provides digital infrastructure and digital solutions to mostly enterprise and hyperscale customers across Africa with its primary operations in broadband connectivity, co-location (data centers), cloud, cybersecurity and payment solutions. 

Finnfund, DFC, and Google have invested together USD 90,000,000 in equity in Cassava Technologies to support Cassava’s effort to expand its digital infrastructure and enhance connectivity across the continent, connecting millions of individuals and businesses to the internet.

Save the Children Myanmar started the Dawn Microfinance Program in 2002. Over the following 13 years, Dawn became a successful microfinance program lending to women-owned businesses in the peri-urban areas of Yangon. In March 2015, the program was transformed into a regulated microfinance company, capitalised by Accion, FMO, and Triodos.
Today, Early Dawn Microfinance Company Limited serves over 200,000 clients through 61 branches in six regions across Myanmar. In terms of client outreach, DAWN is the third-largest MFI in Myanmar. The fast growth of DAWN’s loan portfolio, 82% CAGR since 2016, reflects the country's huge market potential for the microfinance industry.

Export Trading Group (ETG) is a large and diversified agricultural commodity trader and processor with most of its operations in Africa. ETG has about 70 direct subsidiaries serving more than 40 countries on five continents.
ETG is one of Africa's largest players in agribusiness trading and processing. Several major DFIs are funding its operations, and it is widely considered one of Africa's most bankable agribusinesses. DEG is arranging a USD 150 million senior unsecured long-term working capital facility for ETG to improve the balance sheet structurally and enhance trading growth. The DEG-arranged facility will be contractually earmarked for Africa, and Finnfund’s proceeds will be used in Tanzania, Malawi, and Mozambique in five ETG subsidiaries.

Cibuk is the largest wind project in Serbia to date. It is located 45 kilometres northeast of Belgrade, covering 3700 hectares of land partially owned and leased. The 158 MW wind farm will consist of 57 GE turbines and produce up to 475 GWh of electricity annually.

description: Australis Aquaculture Vietnam Ltd is part of Australis Group, which focuses on Barramundi farming. Established in 2007, the company is the largest Barramundi producer in Vietnam. It operates in Van Phong Bay in Khanh Hoa province. A local company processes the grown fish, and the frozen end-product is mainly sold to the USA and Australia, and the by-products are sold to the local market in Vietnam. The company emphasises the sustainability of its operations and has secured many international certifications and awards, as well as retailer-specific certifications. The company plans to increase its production from 3,000 mt to 10-12,000 mt by 2020.

description:
Africado operates Kifufu and Gararagua farms in the Kilimanjaro region in Tanzania, where it cultivates and processes avocados. Africado has 310 hectares of irrigated Hass and mixed avocado species plantations and a modern packhouse. Resource-efficient farming practices are used, and, e.g. the water usage is well below the industry average globally.
The Company has also an extensive smallholder scheme through which the local farmers have been trained and certified, and market access to their produce is ensured. The avocados are exported mainly to Europe.
To expand and diversify the production, the additional funding will be used to plant the Gararagua farm's unplanted area and develop a new Mwanza farm planting macadamia trees.

Africa’s power grids face significant challenges, with utilities struggling to provide consistent service due to outdated infrastructure and unreliable data. Beacon Power Services (BPS) is an energy tech company that provides data-driven solutions that are based on, for example, AI-enabled digital mapping. The funding will enable BPS to enhance its product offerings, support growth in its current operations, and expand into new markets across Eastern and Southern Africa.

African Development Partners III (ADP III) is a private equity fund seeking to invest across Africa.

The Fund is the third-generation PE fund of Development Partners International (DPI). DPIs strategy is to build a diversified pan-African portfolio of private equity investments in established and growing companies benefiting from Africas fast-growing middle class.

ADP III will contribute to creating value within its investees and their positive impact on their local communities, creating more jobs and increasing tax revenues.

BOPA is a holding company established in Singapore in 2013 by private individuals. It invests in regulated small (Tier 2 and 3) microfinance institutions (MFI) in Asia. The MFIs target underserved populations who would not otherwise have access to financial services. A large share of the MFIs’ clientele is female entrepreneurs and the rural population.
Currently, BOPA’s estimated market value of its investment portfolio is USD 35 million and consists of 8 investments located in Kazakhstan, India, Myanmar, Kyrgyzstan, Cambodia, Vietnam, and East Timor. Finnfund participated in BOPA’s fundraising round with an investment of USD 3 million in 2017 and invested a further USD 1,5 million in 2018.
BOPA seeks to invest in MFIs where it sees potential to develop the institution through good corporate governance, funding and efficient IT solutions to become a leading sustainable and socially responsible MFI in its region. The purpose of the latest fundraising round is to invest in selected existing portfolio companies and potentially in new companies.

African Forestry Impact Platform (AFIP) is an evergreen platform managed by the New Forests Asia (Singapore) Ltd. with the intention to establish a large, long-term, value-creation-focused investment vehicle that enables the next phase of growth in Sub-Saharan African forestry.

AfricInvest Fund IV is a pan-African fund focusing on companies across Africa where the Fund has a local presence. The Fund will continue to invest in line with the investment policy and targets of the previous AfricInvest funds and concentrate on familiar sectors. The focus sectors are financial services, manufacturing, fast-moving consumer goods, agribusiness, healthcare, education, and logistics.

Agri-Vie Fund III is a food & agribusiness investment fund in Sub-Saharan Africa with a vision to build businesses in Africa that deliver enviable returns – mindful of the impact on people and the environment.

description:
Arbaro Fund is a private equity fund that invests in sustainable forestry in Latin America and Sub-Saharan Africa.

The fund is managed by Arbaro Advisors GmbH, which employs the fund's management team. The Arbaro Advisors GmbH is owned by forest consulting and management company Unique and asset advisory company Finance in motion.

Finnfund has invested in project company Toplana Zenica d.o.o. Zenica. Steel manufacturer ArcelorMittal Zenica d.o.o. in Bosnia and Herzegovina, city of Zenica, KPA Unicon Oy and Finnfund will form a joint venture project company Toplana Zenica to modernise and upgrade the power generation unit of ArcelorMittal Zenica so that the upgraded unit will be fueled with by-product gases from ArcelorMittal Zenica’s steel manufacturing.
Toplana Zenica will sell district heat to the city of Zenica, steam to ArcelorMittal Zenica and electricity to third parties. KPA Unicon is also the major equipment provider.

The project company was founded to construct and operate a 50 MW solar power plant in Benban, South Egypt. The solar PV power plant is one of about 30 plants to be built on the same 3,700-hectare site in Benban. The Benban site’s total power production will be around 1.5 GW. Electricity produced in the plant will be sold to the government-owned Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company with a long-term power purchase agreement, benefitting the people of Egypt with low-cost renewable electricity.

Satin Creditcare is one of the leading NBFC-MFI microfinance institutions in India catering to low-income families and microbusinesses in rural areas, spanning its journey of more than three decades. As of end December 2025, the company had consolidated assets of USD 1.5 billion with 3.3 million women clients, ranking among the top MFIs in the country. The company operates through diversification in products and geographic presence, aiming to be the ultimate one-stop financial services provider in rural India.

The financing will support Satin Creditcare Network Limited’s inclusive lending activities in India, with a focus on on‑lending to low‑income women borrowers, while strengthening long‑term funding and ESG‑aligned growth.

Finnfund, the Finnish development financier and impact investor, and OeEB, the Development Bank of Austria, are jointly investing USD 25 million in CRDB Bank Burundi, a subsidiary of Tanzania’s largest bank, CRDB Bank Plc. The investment is supported by the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) guarantee, enabling financing in one of the world’s most vulnerable and underserved markets.

Africado was established in 2007 as Tanzania’s first commercial and international-grade producer of avocados. Since then, it has developed the business of producing and exporting Hass avocados. The company farms 137 hectares at Kifufu Estate around the Kilimanjaro area in Tanzania and contracts other commercial and smallholder farmers to supplement its production. To achieve premium quality fruit, the avocados must be handled to a high standard so Africado built and operates a fully operational packhouse at Kifufu Estate, where all the fruit is packaged and exported, primarily to the EU.
Africado is developing the business and starting the production in a new farm, Gararagua, with an avocado orchard of 175 hectares. Africado aims to expand the harvest season and increase the economic scale of its operations. The project also encompasses the expansion of the capacity of the existing packhouse.

Transvolt is a pioneering force in India's electric vehicle (EV) revolution, owning and operating a diverse fleet of EV trucks tippers, trailers, and buses. With a strong presence in states like Maharashtra, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, and beyond, Transvolt is driving the shift toward eco-friendly transportation solutions. The company's advanced EV fleet is designed to meet the demands of modern logistics, construction, and public transport, offering efficient, cost-effective, and emission-free alternatives to traditional vehicles. Transvolt's EV trucks and tippers cater to heavy-duty industries, while its EV buses provide clean, comfortable commuting options for urban and rural areas. Finnfund's financing helps Transvolt to grow.

СJSC MCC Bailyk Finance is a top-3 leading microfinance institution in the Kyrgyz Republic with a 12% market share by the loan portfolio size. Founded in 2010, the institution has a clear social mission: providing accessible financial solutions to residents of rural areas and small towns to improve their quality of life.
Bailyk Finance serves over 62,000 active borrowers through 54 regional branches, with a gross loan portfolio of USD 85 million and maintains strong financial metrics. Bailyk Finance employs over 700 staff, 73% of whom are women, with 89% based in the regions. Gender equality is embedded at every level of the organisation - 50% of the senior management team and 60% of the Board of Directors are women.

Responsible lending is reinforced through financial literacy trainings, ensuring borrowers have the skills to manage credit effectively. Beyond credit, 74% of clients are covered by insurance – with total payouts growing 3.5 times in recent years – and the “My Doctor” online platform extends access to healthcare in rural areas. Bailyk Finance is making steady progress on its environmental commitments: over 95% of loans are processed via electronic digital signatures, offices are transitioning to solar panels, and it is actively growing its green loan portfolio to support environmentally responsible client practices.

The investment supports Finnfund’s mission to expand financial inclusion in underserved markets. In Kyrgyzstan, the majority of low‑income and rural clients lack access to longer‑tenor financing, as local banks primarily offer short‑term funding. 77% of Bailyk Finance’s clients live in rural and semi‑urban areas, and 56% of the portfolio is directed to agricultural borrowers which is nearly three times the national microfinance sector average.

Miro Forestry Developments Limited is a forestry company with two subsidiaries in Ghana and Sierra Leone. Miro is a vertically integrated, sustainable forestry and timber products business focused on fast-growing, high-yield plantation timber to produce sawn timber, utility poles and plywood for local and international markets.
Miro has demonstrated competence in land preparation, planting, forestry management and species selection, successfully planting ca. 20,000 hectares.
Finnfund has invested in Miro since 2014. The new funding is deployed to support the scale up of Miro’s downstream processing capacity, particularly plywood.

Kashf Foundation is an existing client of Finnfund. This is the third loan to Kashf to continue on-lending business loans to its customers. Kashf's loan portfolio has grown steadily and without sacrificing high-quality loan issuance to its customers. Kashf is registered as a Non-Banking Micro Finance Company, and it is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Its customers are low-income households, especially women, who account to over 95% of its borrowers. Financial services include appraisal-backed individual lending, along with other non-financial services that have a transformative impact at the household level. Non-financial services include capacity building by offering skills development training to better understand the products and services, and tele-health clinics.

Ecobank is present in 33 African countries and employs around 14,000 people. Ecobank mandated Bank of Africa United Kingdom to arrange USD 150 million three-year term facility agreement to finance trade finance and related activities.

Finnfund participated in a follow-on mezzanine (convertible loan) investment in Oasis Credit (Mikrokredit Tashkiloti Oasiscredit (Oasis)), an existing microfinance institution in Uzbekistan. The investment supports the company’s capital base and growth of its loan portfolio, enabling increased access to finance for micro and small enterprises, particularly family-owned businesses and underserved entrepreneurs. The round aims to strengthen Oasis Credit’s path to profitability and prepare the company for a future equity fundraising round.

WorldLink Communications is the largest private sector internet service provider in Nepal and one of the most prominent IT companies in the country. Finnfund's investment will be used to expand the existing fibre network in urban and rural areas and to build the company’s first colocation data centre in Kathmandu.

ATB is a 20 MW rice-husk-fired renewable energy power plant operating in Thailand. The power plant is located in one of the key rice-growing areas of Thailand. The project started commercial operations in December 2005, and Finnfund has been a shareholder in ATB since it was established.

client_name: Finnfund Digital Access Impact Fund I LP
description: Finnfund Digital Access Impact Fund is an equity fund focused on digital infrastructure and solutions in emerging and frontier markets. The investments are targeted towards the regions and digital subsectors with the most attractive risk-return potential while focusing on creating positive social impact. In addition to financial return, the Fund aims to increase digital, financial, and gender inclusion with its investments.

Poa is a low-cost home internet service provider offering highly affordable broadband internet services at speeds of up to 5 Mbps for a fixed monthly or weekly pre-paid subscription to underserved urban communities in Kenya. Through this investment, Finnfund will support Poa in expanding its offering to more homes in Kenya and deploying additional technologies in its network, including fiber.

Access Bank is an existing client of Finnfund. The loan is to refinance the already matured and repaid loan, strengthen the bank’s Tier II capital base, and support its MSME on-lending activities in Nigeria.

It currently has presence in 14 cities and has gained an average market share of 25 per cent within a few months of operation.

In 2013, BII (then CDC Group) provided a $25 million loan to Grameenphone. We are providing $10 million in debt financing to Grow Indigo, via our Kinetic Climate Innovation Facility. Grow Indigo aims to transform the Indian smallholder agricultural sector with more sustainable, regenerative practices. The company does this by creating sustainable products and solutions that help optimise these smallholders’ yields, enhance their incomes and reduce resource wastage.  Our investment will be used by Grow Indigo to onboard smallholder farmers across 14 states in India. Grow Indigo will work with them to adopt regenerative agricultural practices. These initiatives will help enhance soil health, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, prevent soil erosion, preserve biodiversity and improve water efficiency.  The project will have an important demonstration effect on the potential for carbon credits to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from traditional agriculture and support increased soil carbon stocks.

In partnership with Norfund and IndiGrid, we launched EnerGrid, a $300 million platform to develop greenfield transmission and standalone battery energy storage system projects in India. IndiGrid is India’s largest listed transmission sector focused Infrastructure Investment Trust. IndiGrid brings its home-grown understanding of the Indian power transmission sector to the partnership, and BII and Norfund provide access to capital (BII has committed $98 million). The transaction is structured uniquely with an assured buy-out of BII and Norfund’s investment by IndiGrid after projects become operational. The aim is to help attract commercial capital into the transmission sector in India.

We initially committed ZAR 240 million to H1 Capital in 2021 to allow the company to scale and add up to 2.4 gigawatts gross capacity of new renewable projects in South Africa. We made a follow on commitment of a further ZAR 467.5 million in 2022. This is mezzanine financing to fund H1 Capital's share of equity requirements of three solar plus battery projects in Kenhardt, South Africa that the company is developing along with Scatec, a leading renewable energy solutions provider.  86 per cent of South Africa’s energy generation comes from fossil fuel; coal is the primary baseload technology (74 per cent) followed by gas (6 per cent) and diesel (6 per cent). As a result, the power sector contributes more than half of the country’s greenhouse gas emissions. Our investment helps contribute to the decarbonisation of a highly emitting power sector and assist in meeting power shortages in the country.

In a country where over 20 million people do not have a bank account, our investment will help people on low incomes access financial services. We provided a loan to Habib Bank Ltd (HBL) to support farmers and agribusinesses in Pakistan by providing improved access to essential financing and enhancing their resilience to climate change. With our loan, HBL plans to expand its agriculture portfolio, dedicating 50 per cent of the funds to smallholder farmers who constitute over 90 per cent of Pakistan's farming population.

The facility will increase HBL UK's capacity to support trade with local banks and trade supply chains across South Asia and Africa, particularly in markets where HBL UK has a strong regional footprint (i.e. Pakistan and Bangladesh).  It will increase the availability of trade finance in the market through supporting HBL UK in re-building its trade book. This will enable domestic businesses to import the commodities and capital equipment they need to sustain and potentially increase business operations, market output and contribution to GDP. Ultimately, it will lead to the retention of jobs and livelihoods, and the continued or increased availability of goods and services in the market.

description: We invested $20 million in a three-year senior unsecured green bond issued by Ho Chi Minh City Development Joint Stock Commercial Bank (HDBank), one of Vietnam’s leading private sector commercial banks. The investment forms part of a $100 million green bond issuance led by IFC and co-subscribed by other development finance institutions. The bond will be used to support HDBank’s lending into climate-eligible sectors in Vietnam, providing longer-tenor foreign currency funding to diversify the bank’s liability profile and strengthen its asset-liability management.

Among multilateral development banks and DFIs, BII is an early provider of debt financing for smart metering projects in India. This investment will support improved grid efficiency and enhance the quality of service for customers in the context of growing electricity demand. Smart metering can also contribute to lower greenhouse gas emissions by reducing technical losses and improving system efficiency. In addition, it enables better integration of renewable energy through tools such as time-of-use tariffs, helping to balance demand throughout the day.

Our financing will support the construction of nine solar power plants at the Benban Solar Park, contributing to 390MW of capacity.

We partnered with IFC on their global trade programme for Ukraine. This $25 million risk sharing facility has been established specifically to support trade flow of essential goods into Ukraine. The facility aims to directly contribute to unlocking commercial trade between Ukraine and the rest of the world by restoring bank-to-bank intermediation, which is necessary for international trade but had become unavailable to Ukraine since the start of the war. In addition, the facility will support the restoration of Ukraine’s own trade flow which has also been critically affected by the war; including the country’s ability to source essential commodities so sustain livelihoods. The facility will bridge the trade finance gap as there is a limited number of confirming banks and guarantee providers in Ukraine.

BII has provided a $40 million commitment to Indorama in Nigeria to enable its subsidiaries (Indorama Eleme Fertilizers and Chemical Limited and Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals Limited) to purchase equipment and implement processes that reduce greenhouse gases, recover heat and improve effluent treatment. This will support Indorama to reduce its emissions and increase water-use efficiency. The investment will support Indorama to reduce emissions at its Nigerian fertiliser plants by up to 348 million tCO2e per annum by 2026 (a 15 per cent reduction from its 2022 baseline). Our funding will also help the business reduce its annual water consumption by 635m3/hour, easing pressure on groundwater aquifers.

We first made a $40 million loan to the company in 2013 and followed that up with $100 million loan in 2018. Those loans were to support the construction of this fertilizer manufacturer, with the aim of helping Nigeria, which is heavily dependent on imported fertilizer, to become self-sufficient. In 2020, we provided additional debt financing of $25 million for the construction of a feed conditioning unit to be installed as part of one of Indorama’s fertiliser production lines. The unit will separate the heavier hydrocarbons from the feed gas and provide a steady, methane-rich feed gas to Indorama’s fertiliser plant. The heavy hydrocarbons are then used as a feed for production of polyolefins at Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals Ltd. The feed conditioning unit will save 70,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year, recovering CO2 that would otherwise be vented.

Our investment will support Agristar's existing operations, the roll out of regenerative agriculture practices across its farms and the installation of solar-powered irrigation pumps. As part of the transaction we also rolled up our stake in Jacoma Estates, a macadamia nut farming operation in Malawi, into Agristar. This is an equity investment in Namdev Finvest Private Limited where we co-invested alongside Incofin India Progress Fund I.  Namdev is a lender focused on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), based in Rajasthan, India. It provides secured loans to customers in rural areas who are new to credit (approximately 30 per cent) or have limited credit history (approximately 70 per cent). The company offers loans for predominantly income-generating assets and is active through two main products: MSME loans (87 per cent) and two-wheeler loans (11 per cent). Namdev recently launched a first electric vehicle/solar loan product, financed by the Symbiotics Green Basket Bond (backed by BII) which it plans to scale over the next few years. The company is highly focused on rural lending and scaling up its green financing portfolio. Its data suggests that 66 per cent of its customers have monthly household incomes below INR 28,000 (BII’s low-income proxy for India). Furthermore, because many of Namdev’s customers are new to credit, this supports financial and economic inclusion, as lower-income individuals are less likely to secure finance from traditional lenders. Namdev also has women as primary applicants on 30 per cent of its loans and women are mandatory co-applicants on all loans. As part of the overall fundraise, our capital will help support Namdev’s growth including an increase in Namdev’s loan book, geographic expansion, and employment base. We are having financial additionality by helping Namdev successfully complete the fundraising round.

The green bond investment will support small and medium enterprises involved in climate financing projects, create jobs and accelerate the country’s energy transition to support greenhouse gas emissions reduction.

Obelisk is a large-scale renewable energy project in Egypt, led by Scatec. Our financing will support the development of a 1GWac (1.125GWp) solar photovoltaic (PV) plant, integrated with a 100MW/200MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). Located in Nagaa Hammadi in the Qena Governorate, the project aims to enhance energy security and support Egypt’s transition to clean energy.
